    Algorithms¶

    Every algorithm of tack.dataset, by what it does, with its parameters. Each group opens with a table: what each algorithm gives, what it takes (a DataSet; pieces, a PartitionedDataSet, over MPI ranks or not; an AMRDataSet; an OctreeDataSet), and its nearest counterpart in VTK and in Viskores. Below the table, each algorithm's signature and description.

    import tack.dataset as td

hot = td.threshold(data, "temperature", 300.0, 400.0)
grad = td.gradients(data, "pressure", at="points")
s = td.statistics(data, "pressure")

    Every algorithm is in tack.dataset.algorithms, one module each, and tack.dataset re-exports them all. They share conventions, set out in the Dataset API reference's Algorithms and filters:

    • the dataset comes first, and a field argument is a Field or the name of one of the dataset's fields;
    • an algorithm that makes a new dataset takes fields=: which fields to carry (all by default, a name, a list of names, or [] for none), carried by the rules in how fields carry through filters;
    • an algorithm that computes a field returns a Field, several fields a named tuple of them, a summary Python numbers, a selection a Set;
    • nothing changes its input, except where an entry says "in place";
    • every algorithm runs, and allocates, on its dataset's device; algorithms over pieces run each piece on its own device;
    • hidden cells are never processed, and ghost cells and points are left out of summaries;
    • a parameter that is a length, a time or a field's value (a radius, a step size, a threshold's range) also takes a quantity ("10 cm", (10, "cm")), converted to the dataset's or the field's unit; a plain number is taken as it is (Units).

    Which algorithms work on which topologies (polyhedra, polygons, polylines) is in the Dataset API reference's support table. The classes the algorithms take and give -- datasets, fields, spaces, topologies, sets, implicit functions, locators -- are in Data Model.

    Contents¶

    • Cells kept whole: New datasets of some of the input's cells, unchanged, with only the points they use.
    • Cutting: New datasets of pieces of cells, with points made on their edges.
    • Surfaces and edges: A mesh's faces and edges, as sets or datasets on the same points.
    • Connectivity and winding: Which cells belong together, and which are wound wrong.
    • Changing cell types: The same points and region, in other cells.
    • Moving the geometry: New positions for the same topology.
    • Measures and quality: Fields describing the mesh itself.
    • Fields from fields: New fields computed from a dataset's fields.
    • Finite volumes: Values on faces and the cells around them.
    • Summaries: Python numbers about a field, over every piece and rank.
    • Probing, sampling and particles: Values at other points, and paths through a velocity field.
    • Point clouds: Points as vertex cells: neighbours found through a PointLocator.
    • Pieces and ghosts: A PartitionedDataSet's pieces, over MPI ranks or not.
    • Adaptive mesh refinement: Algorithms only an AMRDataSet takes; ghost_cells, probe, statistics and the rest above take one too.

    Cells kept whole¶

    New datasets of some of the input's cells, unchanged, with only the points they use.

    Algorithm Gives Takes VTK Viskores
    threshold cells whose field lies in a range dataset vtkThreshold Threshold
    extract_cells cells by id, array or cell set dataset vtkExtractCells —
    extract_geometry cells inside (or outside, or cut by) an implicit function dataset vtkExtractGeometry ExtractGeometry

    threshold ¶

    threshold(
    data,
    field,
    lower,
    upper,
    all_points=True,
    fields=None,
    subdivision=None,
    tolerance=None,
)

    The cells whose field lies in [lower, upper], with only the points they use.

    field is a scalar field or its name. A cell field (Constant, values on cells) keeps a cell by its value; a field with a basis (H1, L2; above order 1 or on curved cells, see below) or values on points by its values at the cell's corners: all of them in range, or with all_points=False any (VTK's AllScalars). The result's cells keep their shapes and order; its points are the used ones, renumbered in order. Every field it can carry comes along: point fields gathered to the kept points, cell fields to the kept cells, L2 fields (and an L2 geometry) block by block, keeping each cell's order. Fields on faces and edges, which the new topology derives afresh, are left behind.

    On a polyhedral topology the kept cells keep their faces, stored once and numbered in their old order, so values on faces come along. A face whose side-0 cell is dropped is turned around for its remaining cell, and its oriented values (Values(..., "faces", oriented=True)) are negated. A polygonal topology's kept polygons keep their loops, and a polyline topology's polylines their chains; their facets' values, whose numbering is derived afresh, are left behind.

    A curved geometry or a field above order 1 (or subdivision above 1, or a tolerance) is thresholded through subdivision, and the result is PartitionedDataSet([whole, part]): whole the cells whose field's Bernstein bound lies in the range, as they are (curved, their fields of any order), and part the threshold of the sub-cells of the others whose bound meets it, each cut into subdivision lattice steps (by default the largest order of the field and the geometry; with tolerance, in the field's unit, the fewest whose estimated error is within it).

    @on_inputs_device
def threshold(data, field, lower, upper, all_points=True, fields=None, subdivision=None,
              tolerance=None):
    """The cells whose ``field`` lies in ``[lower, upper]``, with only the points they use.

    ``field`` is a scalar field or its name. A cell field (``Constant``, values
    on cells) keeps a cell by its value; a field with a basis (``H1``, ``L2``;
    above order 1 or on curved cells, see below) or values on points by its
    values at the cell's corners:
    all of them in range, or with ``all_points=False`` any (VTK's
    ``AllScalars``). The result's cells keep their shapes and order; its points
    are the used ones, renumbered in order. Every field it can carry comes
    along: point fields gathered to the kept points, cell fields to the kept
    cells, ``L2`` fields (and an ``L2`` geometry) block by block, keeping each
    cell's order. Fields on faces and edges, which the new topology derives
    afresh, are left behind.

    On a polyhedral topology the kept cells keep their faces, stored once and
    numbered in their old order, so values on faces come along. A face whose
    side-0 cell is dropped is turned around for its remaining cell, and its
    oriented values (``Values(..., "faces", oriented=True)``) are negated. A
    polygonal topology's kept polygons keep their loops, and a polyline
    topology's polylines their chains; their facets' values, whose numbering is
    derived afresh, are left behind.

    A curved geometry or a field above order 1 (or ``subdivision`` above 1, or a
    ``tolerance``) is thresholded through subdivision, and the result is
    ``PartitionedDataSet([whole, part])``: ``whole`` the cells whose field's
    Bernstein bound lies in the range, as they are (curved, their fields of any
    order), and ``part`` the threshold of the sub-cells of the others whose bound
    meets it, each cut into ``subdivision`` lattice steps (by default the largest
    order of the field and the geometry; with ``tolerance``, in the field's unit,
    the fewest whose estimated error is within it).
    """
    lower, upper = (_in_unit_of(_field(data, field), v, "threshold's bounds")
                    for v in (lower, upper))
    field = _field(data, field)
    if arrays.width_of(field.values):
        raise TypeError("threshold needs a scalar field")
    field = _with_basis(data, field)
    space = field.space
    if not space.interpolated or space.on not in ("cells", "points"):
        raise TypeError(f"threshold needs a field on the points or cells, not {space!r}")
    from tack.dataset.algorithms.subdivide import split_by_range, subdivides

    by_cells = isinstance(space, Constant) or (space.on == "cells"
                                               and not isinstance(space, (H1, L2)))
    if not by_cells and getattr(data.topology, "reference_cells", True) and (
            subdivides(data, field) or tolerance is not None
            or (subdivision is not None and subdivision > 1)):
        from tack.dataset.ghosts import visible

        data, field = visible(data, field)
        if tolerance is not None:
            tolerance = _in_unit_of(field, tolerance, "threshold's tolerance")
        return split_by_range(
            data, field, lower, upper, subdivision, tolerance, fields,
            lambda refined, name, carried: threshold(refined, name, lower, upper, all_points,
                                                      carried))
    return _keep_cells(data, _threshold_flags(data, field, lower, upper, all_points), fields)

    @on_inputs_device
def extract_cells(data, cells, fields=None):
    """The cells with the given ids (a host array, an integer field, or a cell
    ``Set`` or its name in ``data.sets``), with only the points they use; cells
    keep their order, not the order given."""
    from tack.dataset.sets import Set

    if isinstance(cells, str):
        cells = data.sets[cells]
    if isinstance(cells, Set):
        if cells.on != "cells" or cells.topology is not data.topology:
            raise ValueError(f"extract_cells takes a set of this dataset's cells, not a "
                             f"set of {cells.on}" + ("" if cells.topology is data.topology
                                                    else " of another topology"))
        cells = cells.ids
    if not hasattr(cells, "numpy"):
        values = np.asarray(cells).reshape(-1)
        if values.size and not np.issubdtype(values.dtype, np.integer):
            raise TypeError("cell ids must be integers")
        cells = values
    chosen = ids.as_ids(cells, data.id_dtype)
    keep = tack.zeros((data.num_cells,), tack.i32)
    if chosen.shape[0]:
        ids.check_bounds(chosen, data.num_cells, "cell")
        _flag_ids(chosen, keep)
    return _keep_cells(data, keep, fields)

    @on_inputs_device
def extract_geometry(data, function, inside=True, boundary=False, fields=None):
    """The whole cells inside ``function``'s region (all their points at or below zero),
    or, with ``inside=False``, outside it (all above); with ``boundary``, also the
    cells it cuts (some point on the kept side). Cells are not split -- that is
    clip. Points are compacted and fields carried, as by ``threshold``."""

    values = implicit_values(data, function)
    if inside:
        return threshold(data, values, -np.inf, 0.0, all_points=not boundary, fields=fields)
    # Outside is what is not inside, exactly: all points above zero is no point at
    # or below it, and some point above is not all at or below.
    keep = _threshold_flags(data, values, -np.inf, 0.0, all_points=boundary)
    _complement(keep)
    return _keep_cells(data, keep, fields)

    extract_extent ¶

    extract_extent(data, extent, rate=1, fields=None)

    The points of data, a structured grid, in the box extent -- one (low, high) pair of point indices per axis, both included, or VTK's flat (i0, i1, j0, j1, k0, k1), in the whole grid's indices (as VTK's extents count them, from the topology's offset), clipped to the grid -- every rate-th along each axis (a number, or one per axis): a structured grid of the same kind, an image's coordinates still uniform, a rectilinear grid's axes cut, explicit points taken. VTK's vtkExtractGrid.

    An axis of one point is dropped: a k-plane of a 3D grid is a 2D grid, whose cells are faces of the 3D grid's. Point fields come along at the points kept; each cell takes the cell fields, marks and ids of the input cell at its first corner -- the cell beyond a plane, or before it at the grid's far side -- as VTK takes them. The output's offset is its first point's index, so its extent is the box's (with rate 1).

    @on_inputs_device
def extract_extent(data, extent, rate=1, fields=None):
    """The points of ``data``, a structured grid, in the box ``extent`` -- one
    (low, high) pair of point indices per axis, both included, or VTK's flat
    (i0, i1, j0, j1, k0, k1), in the whole grid's indices (as VTK's extents
    count them, from the topology's ``offset``), clipped to the grid -- every
    ``rate``-th along each axis (a number, or one per axis): a structured grid
    of the same kind, an image's coordinates still uniform, a rectilinear
    grid's axes cut, explicit points taken. VTK's ``vtkExtractGrid``.

    An axis of one point is dropped: a k-plane of a 3D grid is a 2D grid,
    whose cells are faces of the 3D grid's. Point fields come along at the
    points kept; each cell takes the cell fields, marks and ids of the input
    cell at its first corner -- the cell beyond a plane, or before it at the
    grid's far side -- as VTK takes them. The output's ``offset`` is its first
    point's index, so its extent is the box's (with ``rate`` 1)."""
    topology = data.topology
    if not isinstance(topology, StructuredTopology):
        raise TypeError("extract_extent takes a structured grid (an image, a rectilinear "
                        "or a curvilinear grid); extract_cells selects any mesh's cells")
    dims = list(topology.point_dims)
    n = len(dims)
    rates = [int(rate)] * n if np.ndim(rate) == 0 else [int(r) for r in rate]
    if len(rates) != n or min(rates) < 1:
        raise ValueError(f"rate is a step of at least 1, or one per axis, not {rate!r}")
    offset = list(topology.offset)
    starts, counts = [], []
    for (lo, hi), d, o, r in zip(_ranges(extent, n), dims, offset, rates, strict=True):
        lo, hi = max(lo, o), min(hi, o + d - 1)
        if hi < lo:
            raise ValueError(f"the extent {extent!r} misses the grid's points "
                             f"{[(o, o + d - 1) for o, d in zip(offset, dims)]}")
        starts.append(lo - o)
        counts.append((hi - lo) // r + 1)
    kept = [a for a in range(n) if counts[a] > 1]
    if not kept:
        raise ValueError(f"the extent {extent!r} holds one point of the grid: no cells")
    out_dims = [counts[a] for a in kept]
    device = data.device
    out = StructuredTopology(out_dims, id_dtype=topology.id_dtype, device=device,
                             offset=[offset[a] + starts[a] for a in kept])
    # Each output cell's first corner, in the input's cells; along a dropped
    # axis, the cell beyond the point, or before it at the far side.
    cells = [d - 1 for d in dims]
    cell_starts = [min(s, c - 1) if counts[a] == 1 else s
                   for a, (s, c) in enumerate(zip(starts, cells))]
    cell_counts = [max(c - 1, 1) for c in counts]
    point_ids = _ids(dims, starts, counts, rates, topology.id_dtype)
    cell_ids = (_ids(cells, cell_starts, cell_counts, rates, topology.id_dtype)
                if out_dims and min(cells) > 0 else tack.empty((0,), topology.id_dtype))
    coordinates = data.geometry.values
    geometry = None
    if isinstance(data.geometry.space, H1) and isinstance(coordinates,
                                                          (UniformCoordinates, CartesianProduct)):
        geometry = Field(H1(out), _strided_geometry(coordinates, starts, counts, rates, device),
                         data.unit)
    return carry(data, out, points=Take(point_ids), cells=Take(cell_ids), geometry=geometry,
                 fields=fields)

    @on_inputs_device
def mask(data, stride, fields=None):
    """Every ``stride``-th cell (0, stride, 2 * stride, ...), as Viskores' ``Mask``,
    with only the points they use: fields carry as ``threshold`` carries them.
    ``mask_points`` is its point twin."""
    if int(stride) < 1:
        raise ValueError(f"stride must be at least 1, not {stride!r}")
    keep = tack.empty((data.num_cells,), tack.i32)
    if data.num_cells:
        _every(keep, int(stride))
    return _keep_cells(data, keep, fields)

    Cutting¶

    New datasets of pieces of cells, with points made on their edges.

    Algorithm Gives Takes VTK Viskores
    contour isosurfaces, isolines or points of a field, one level or several dataset vtkContourFilter Contour
    slice where an implicit function is zero (or a level) dataset vtkCutter Slice
    slice_plane a plane's cut, or parallel planes dataset vtkCutter Slice
    clip the part above (or below) a field's level or inside an implicit function dataset vtkTableBasedClipDataSet ClipWithField, ClipWithImplicitFunction

    contour ¶

    contour(
    data,
    field,
    value,
    merge_points=True,
    fields=None,
    dimension=None,
    subdivision=None,
    tolerance=None,
    exact=True,
)

    Where field crosses value: a surface of a 3D mesh, as triangles (as polygons on polyhedra); lines of a 2D mesh.

    value may be a sequence: the surfaces of every value, in one dataset made in one pass over the cells (each cell compared with every value), with each output cell's value in a cell field contour_value. Points are not shared between values.

    field is a scalar field with a basis, or its name: H1 of order 1 (point data), or L2 (DG, an order per cell too).

    On segments, quads, pixels, hexahedra and voxels, and on triangles, tetrahedra and wedges (into Freudenthal's sub-simplices, a wedge's in layers), a field above order 1 or a curved geometry is cut on linear sub-cells (tack.dataset.subdivide): each cell whose field's Bernstein coefficients can hold a value is cut into subdivision lattice steps along each axis -- by default the largest order of the field and geometry -- and the surface is the sub-cells'; a lattice point shared by cells is evaluated once, so the surface has no cracks. Each crossing of a sub-cell's edge is where the field itself takes the value along it (exact, the default), found from the field's own values on the edge, face or cell holding it, so a vertex lies on the true surface (to rounding) whatever the steps, and neighbouring cells and pieces put it at the same bits; with exact=False, where the line between the lattice values does, as a linear contour of the sub-cells. subdivision=1 with exact=False is the cut of the cells linearized at their corners. tolerance (in the field's unit) chooses the fewest steps whose estimated error is within it instead: what linearizing a cell loses is bounded by its Bernstein coefficients' distance from the corners' interpolation, divided by about the square of the steps; a curved geometry's own bend is not counted. Give one or the other. Elsewhere an order-2 H1 field is refused: its cells would need subdividing, and their corner values alone are another, linear field. Each 3D cell contributes the triangles of VTK's case tables for its corner values, interpolated along its edges; in a mesh with 3D cells, cells of lower dimension contribute nothing, and a cell constant has no level set inside its cells.

    dimension (3, 2 or 1) chooses which cells to contour, by default the mesh's highest: the cells of that dimension alone, as a mesh of their own on the points they use (no cells of it, no contour), so a mesh of tetrahedra and the triangles of its boundary gives the tetrahedra's surface, or with dimension=2 the triangles' lines. Cells of other dimensions are never mixed in.

    A 2D mesh -- triangles, quads, pixels or polygons -- gives line cells from its point values: each cell's crossings, found going round its edges, are joined in pairs, each line with the higher values on its right as the cell winds. Lines share their points through the mesh's faces (its edges), whatever merge_points says -- unless the field or the geometry is L2: then each cell's lines have their own points, from its own values and corners. No cells give no lines.

    A 1D mesh -- lines or polylines -- gives a vertex cell at each crossing of its segments, from its point values, interpolated from the end first by position; a crossing at a point whose value is the level is that point, and with merge_points every crossing is one vertex, each taking the cell fields of the first cell to cross there.

    With merge_points, triangles share their points: by global edge when the field and the geometry are both continuous, so the surface is watertight; otherwise only within each cell, so a DG field's surface keeps its jumps and an L2 geometry's its gaps. H1 fields carry onto the surface's points, interpolated along the same edges; cell fields (Constant, values on cells) onto its triangles, from the cell each came from.

    @on_inputs_device
def contour(data, field, value, merge_points=True, fields=None, dimension=None,
            subdivision=None, tolerance=None, exact=True):
    """Where ``field`` crosses ``value``: a surface of a 3D mesh, as triangles
    (as polygons on polyhedra); lines of a 2D mesh.

    ``value`` may be a sequence: the surfaces of every value, in one dataset
    made in one pass over the cells (each cell compared with every value),
    with each output cell's value in a cell field ``contour_value``. Points
    are not shared between values.

    ``field`` is a scalar field with a basis, or its name: ``H1`` of order 1
    (point data), or ``L2`` (DG, an order per cell too).

    On segments, quads, pixels, hexahedra and voxels, and on triangles,
    tetrahedra and wedges (into Freudenthal's sub-simplices, a wedge's in
    layers), a field above order 1 or a
    curved geometry is cut on linear sub-cells (``tack.dataset.subdivide``): each
    cell whose field's Bernstein coefficients can hold a value is cut into
    ``subdivision`` lattice steps along each axis -- by default the largest
    order of the field and geometry -- and the surface is the sub-cells'; a
    lattice point shared by cells is evaluated once, so the surface has no
    cracks. Each crossing of a sub-cell's edge is where the field itself takes
    the value along it (``exact``, the default), found from the field's own
    values on the edge, face or cell holding it, so a vertex lies on the true
    surface (to rounding) whatever the steps, and neighbouring cells and pieces
    put it at the same bits; with ``exact=False``, where the line between the
    lattice values does, as a linear contour of the sub-cells.
    ``subdivision=1`` with ``exact=False`` is the cut of the cells linearized at
    their corners. ``tolerance`` (in the field's unit) chooses the fewest steps whose
    estimated error is within it instead: what linearizing a cell loses is
    bounded by its Bernstein coefficients' distance from the corners'
    interpolation, divided by about the square of the steps; a curved
    geometry's own bend is not counted. Give one or the other. Elsewhere an order-2 ``H1`` field is refused: its cells would
    need subdividing, and their corner values alone are another, linear field. Each 3D cell contributes the
    triangles of VTK's case tables for its corner values, interpolated along
    its edges; in a mesh with 3D cells, cells of lower dimension contribute
    nothing, and a cell constant has no level set inside its cells.

    ``dimension`` (3, 2 or 1) chooses which cells to contour, by default the
    mesh's highest: the cells of that dimension alone, as a mesh of their own on
    the points they use (no cells of it, no contour), so a mesh of tetrahedra
    and the triangles of its boundary gives the tetrahedra's surface, or with
    ``dimension=2`` the triangles' lines. Cells of other dimensions are never
    mixed in.

    A 2D mesh -- triangles, quads, pixels or polygons -- gives line cells from
    its point values: each cell's crossings, found going round its edges, are
    joined in pairs, each line with the higher values on its right as the
    cell winds. Lines share their points through the mesh's faces (its edges),
    whatever ``merge_points`` says -- unless the field or the geometry is
    ``L2``: then each cell's lines have their own points, from its own values
    and corners. No cells give no lines.

    A 1D mesh -- lines or polylines -- gives a vertex cell at each crossing of
    its segments, from its point values, interpolated from the end first by position;
    a crossing at a point whose value is the level is that point, and with
    ``merge_points`` every crossing is one vertex, each taking the cell fields
    of the first cell to cross there.

    With ``merge_points``, triangles share their points: by global edge when
    the field and the geometry are both continuous, so the surface is
    watertight; otherwise only within each cell, so a DG field's surface
    keeps its jumps and an ``L2`` geometry's its gaps. ``H1`` fields carry
    onto the surface's points, interpolated along the same edges; cell
    fields (``Constant``, values on cells) onto its triangles, from the cell
    each came from.
    """
    value = _in_unit_of(_field(data, field), value, "contour's value")
    from tack.dataset.ghosts import visible

    data, field = visible(data, field)
    field = _field(data, field)
    space = field.space
    from tack.dataset.algorithms.subdivide import subdivided_contour, subdivides

    if tolerance is not None:
        tolerance = _in_unit_of(field, tolerance, "contour's tolerance")
    # Polyhedra, polygons and polylines have no lattice to subdivide: linear,
    # they are cut as they are (as threshold and clip cut them).
    if (dimension is None or dimension == data.topology.dimension) and getattr(
            data.topology, "reference_cells", True) and (
            subdivides(data, field) or (subdivision is not None and subdivision > 1)
            or tolerance is not None):
        _scalar_floating("contour", field)
        levels, nlevels, _ = _levels(value, field)
        return subdivided_contour(
            data, field, value, levels, nlevels, subdivision,
            lambda refined, name: contour(refined, name, value, merge_points=merge_points,
                                          fields=fields, dimension=dimension),
            tolerance=tolerance, exact=exact)
    if isinstance(space, H1) and space.order != 1:
        raise NotImplementedError(
            f"contour of an order-{space.order} H1 field is not built: it would subdivide "
            "each cell, and its corner values alone give the contour of a linear field")
    _scalar_floating("contour", field)
    levels, nlevels, several = _levels(value, field)
    top = data.topology.dimension
    if dimension is None:
        dimension = top if top >= 1 else 3       # no cells (or vertices): no surface
    if dimension not in (1, 2, 3):
        raise ValueError(f"contour's dimension is 3, 2 or 1 (the cells to contour), "
                         f"not {dimension!r}")
    mixed = any(g.count and g.shape.DIMENSION != dimension for g in data.topology.groups())
    if mixed or dimension > top:
        data, field = _cells_of_dimension(data, field, dimension)
    if dimension == 2:
        return _contour_lines(data, field, levels, nlevels, several, fields)
    if dimension == 1:
        return _contour_vertices(data, field, levels, nlevels, several, merge_points, fields)
    if not getattr(data.topology, "reference_cells", True):
        return _polyhedral_contour(data, field, levels, nlevels, several, fields)
    field = _with_basis(data, field)
    space = field.space
    if not space.interpolated or space.on not in ("cells", "points"):
        raise TypeError(f"contour needs a field with a basis on the cells, not {space!r}")
    per_cell = 0 if isinstance(space, H1) and isinstance(data.geometry.space, H1) else 1
    groups = [g for g in data.launch_groups("cells", [field])
              if g.count and g.shape.CONTOUR_TRIANGLES]
    n_cells = data.num_cells
    idt = data.id_dtype
    odt = ids.for_output(data, 15 * n_cells * nlevels)     # up to five triangles a cell
    # Keys hold the level beside a point or cell id.
    kdt = ids.at_least(idt, (n_cells if per_cell else data.num_points) * nlevels)
    counts = tack.zeros((n_cells,), tack.i32)
    for group in groups:
        _contour_counts(data.domain_view("cells", group), field.view(group), levels, nlevels,
                        counts)
    starts, triangles = _scanned(counts, n_cells, odt)

    n = 3 * triangles
    points = tack.empty((n,), tack.vec(3, data.dtype))
    edges = tack.empty((n,), tack.vec(2, idt))
    weights = tack.empty((n,), arrays.dtype_of(field.values))
    sources = tack.empty((n,), idt)
    keys = tack.empty((n,), tack.vec(2, kdt))
    which = tack.empty((n,), tack.i32)
    for group in groups:
        _contour_points(data.domain_view("cells", group), field.view(group), levels, nlevels,
                        per_cell, starts, points, edges, weights, sources, keys, which)
    if triangles:
        keep = tack.empty((triangles,), tack.i32)
        _distinct_triangles(keys, keep)
        slots = tack.empty((triangles,), odt)
        kept = exclusive_scan(keep, slots, triangles)
        if kept < triangles:
            arrays_in = (points, edges, weights, sources, keys, which)
            arrays_out = tuple(_like(a, 3 * kept) for a in arrays_in)
            _kept_triangles(keep, slots, *arrays_in, *arrays_out)
            points, edges, weights, sources, keys, which = arrays_out
            triangles, n = kept, 3 * kept
    triangle_cells = tack.empty((triangles,), idt)
    triangle_levels = tack.empty((triangles,), tack.i32)
    if triangles:
        _triangle_cells(sources, which, triangle_cells, triangle_levels)

    if merge_points and n:
        # A key is the edge's (low, high) points, or (within cells) (cell, local edge),
        # its first part times the levels plus the level.
        order = key_order(keys, (n_cells if per_cell else data.num_points) * nlevels,
                                odt)
        offsets, count = run_offsets(keys, order)
        merged = tack.empty((count,), tack.vec(3, data.dtype))
        merged_edges = tack.empty((count,), tack.vec(2, idt))
        merged_weights = tack.empty((count,), weights.dtype)
        _first_of_runs(order, offsets, points, edges, weights, merged, merged_edges,
                       merged_weights, count)
        rows = tack.empty((n,), odt)
        _run_of_each(order, offsets, rows, count)
        points, edges, weights = merged, merged_edges, merged_weights
    else:
        rows, count = CountingArray(n, dtype=odt), n          # each triangle its own points

    # Every cell a triangle, three points each: the types and offsets are
    # implicit, and the connectivity is the triangles' rows of merged points.
    types, tri_offsets = uniform_cells(shapes.TRIANGLE, triangles, odt)
    surface = UnstructuredTopology(types, tri_offsets, rows, num_points=count)
    return _with_levels(carry(data, surface, points=Interpolate(edges, weights),
                              cells=Pieces(triangle_cells), geometry=Field(H1(surface), points),
                              fields=fields), levels, triangle_levels, several,
                        field.unit)

    @on_inputs_device
def slice(data, function, merge_points=True, fields=None, value=0.0, subdivision=None,
          tolerance=None, exact=True):
    """Where ``function`` (``tack.dataset.implicit``) is ``value`` (zero by default):
    a contour of its values on the geometry, carrying fields as ``contour``
    does (``merge_points`` and ``fields`` are ``contour``'s). ``value`` may be
    a sequence, as ``contour``'s: every level in one
    pass, each output cell's in ``contour_value``. ``slice_plane`` is this
    with a ``Plane``. On a curved geometry (``H1`` above order 1) of segments,
    quads, pixels, hexahedra or voxels the cells are cut on linear sub-cells,
    as ``contour`` cuts them (``subdivision``, ``tolerance``, ``exact``); on
    other cells, linearized at their corners."""
    values = implicit_values(data, function)
    from tack.dataset.algorithms.subdivide import subdivides

    if (isinstance(values.space, H1) and values.space.order != 1
            and not subdivides(data, values)):
        # The function's values at the points: projected into order-1 H1, a
        # continuous field keeps them. contour refuses order 2, so slicing a
        # curved dataset raised.
        values = project(data, values, H1(data))
    return contour(data, values, value, merge_points=merge_points, fields=fields,
                   subdivision=subdivision, tolerance=tolerance, exact=exact)

    @on_inputs_device
def slice_plane(data, origin, normal, merge_points=True, fields=None, value=0.0,
                subdivision=None, tolerance=None, exact=True):
    """The cut of the 3D cells by the plane through ``origin`` with ``normal`` (any
    length), as triangles: ``contour`` at zero of each position's signed distance
    to the plane along ``normal``. The distance is computed in the geometry's own
    space -- per point, or per cell corner for an ``L2`` geometry -- so the cut is
    the cells' own. ``value``, a signed distance along the unit normal, or a
    sequence of them, gives parallel planes, all in one pass. ``slice`` with a
    ``Plane``; ``merge_points``, ``fields``, ``subdivision``, ``tolerance`` (a
    distance) and ``exact`` are ``contour``'s."""
    origin = _length(data, origin, "slice_plane's origin")
    value = _length(data, value, "slice_plane's distance")
    if tolerance is not None:
        tolerance = _length(data, tolerance, "slice_plane's tolerance")
    return slice(data, Plane(origin, normal), merge_points=merge_points, fields=fields,
                 value=value, subdivision=subdivision, tolerance=tolerance, exact=exact)

    The part of data where by -- point data (a field or its name) or an implicit function (tack.dataset.implicit) -- is at or above value, or with inside below it: Viskores' ClipWithField and (value 0) ClipWithImplicitFunction, by its case tables. Cells wholly kept keep their shape; cut cells become the pieces their case lists. Points are the kept corners, the crossings on cut edges (merged across cells) and centroid points; point data is interpolated onto them, cell data goes to each piece.

    A polyhedral topology is clipped cell by cell into polyhedra: each cut cell becomes the polyhedron of its kept part, its faces clipped (each face once, so faces two cells share stay one face) and its iso-polygons -- as contour traces them, by López's method -- as caps wound out of it; the output is a PolyhedralTopology. A point at exactly value is kept on either side (inside keeps at or below). Polygons and polylines are not clipped yet.

    A curved geometry or a field above order 1 (or subdivision above 1, or a tolerance) is clipped through subdivision, as contour cuts it, and the result is PartitionedDataSet([whole, part]): whole the cells the field's Bernstein bound keeps entirely, as they are (curved, their fields of any order), and part the clip of the others that the bound does not drop, cut into subdivision lattice steps (by default the largest order of the field and the geometry; with tolerance, in the field's unit, the fewest whose estimated error is within it). The two meet at the lattice points of the faces between them, where a linear sub-face lies against a curved face. The cut's points on sub-cells' edges are where the field takes the value along them (exact, as contour's), or with exact=False where the line between the lattice values does.

    @on_inputs_device
def clip(data, by, value=0.0, inside=False, fields=None, subdivision=None, tolerance=None,
         exact=True):
    """The part of ``data`` where ``by`` -- point data (a field or its name) or an
    implicit function (``tack.dataset.implicit``) -- is at or above ``value``, or
    with ``inside`` below it: Viskores' ClipWithField and (``value`` 0)
    ClipWithImplicitFunction, by its case tables. Cells wholly kept keep their
    shape; cut cells become the pieces their case lists. Points are the kept
    corners, the crossings on cut edges (merged across cells) and centroid
    points; point data is interpolated onto them, cell data goes to each piece.

    A polyhedral topology is clipped cell by cell into polyhedra: each cut cell
    becomes the polyhedron of its kept part, its faces clipped (each face once,
    so faces two cells share stay one face) and its iso-polygons -- as
    ``contour`` traces them, by López's method -- as caps wound out of it; the
    output is a ``PolyhedralTopology``. A point at exactly ``value`` is kept on
    either side (``inside`` keeps at or below). Polygons and polylines are not
    clipped yet.

    A curved geometry or a field above order 1 (or ``subdivision`` above 1, or a
    ``tolerance``) is clipped through subdivision, as ``contour`` cuts it, and the
    result is ``PartitionedDataSet([whole, part])``: ``whole`` the cells the field's
    Bernstein bound keeps entirely, as they are (curved, their fields of any order),
    and ``part`` the clip of the others that the bound does not drop, cut into
    ``subdivision`` lattice steps (by default the largest order of the field and the
    geometry; with ``tolerance``, in the field's unit, the fewest whose estimated
    error is within it). The two meet at the lattice points of the faces between
    them, where a linear sub-face lies against a curved face. The cut's points
    on sub-cells' edges are where the field takes the value along them
    (``exact``, as ``contour``'s), or with ``exact=False`` where the line
    between the lattice values does."""
    from tack.dataset.ghosts import visible

    data, by = visible(data, by)
    from tack.dataset.polyhedra import PolygonalTopology, PolyhedralTopology

    polyhedral = isinstance(data.topology, PolyhedralTopology) and \
        not isinstance(data.topology, PolygonalTopology)
    if not polyhedral and not getattr(data.topology, "reference_cells", True):
        raise NotImplementedError("clip takes cells of the linear shapes or polyhedra, not "
                                  "polygons or polylines")
    implicit = hasattr(by, "value") and not isinstance(by, (str, Field))
    field = implicit_values(data, by) if implicit else _field(data, by)
    # In the field's unit; an implicit function's values have none.
    value = _in_unit_of(field, value, "clip's value")
    if arrays.width_of(field.values):
        raise TypeError("clip needs a scalar field")
    from tack.dataset.algorithms.subdivide import split_by_range, subdivides

    if not polyhedral and (subdivides(data, field) or tolerance is not None
                           or (subdivision is not None and subdivision > 1)):
        if tolerance is not None:
            tolerance = _in_unit_of(field, tolerance, "clip's tolerance")
        bound = float("inf")
        lower, upper = (-bound, value) if inside else (value, bound)
        levels = tack.array(np.asarray([value], arrays.dtype_of(field.values).numpy_dtype))
        return split_by_range(data, field, lower, upper, subdivision, tolerance, fields,
                              lambda refined, name, carried: clip(refined, name, value, inside,
                                                                    carried),
                              levels if exact else None)
    if not isinstance(data.geometry.space, H1):
        # Clip's points are merged across cells, so each needs one position.
        raise TypeError("clip needs an H1 geometry: one position per point")
    space = field.space
    if not implicit and not (isinstance(space, H1)
                             or (isinstance(space, Values) and space.on == "points")):
        raise TypeError(f"clip takes point data or an implicit function, not {space!r}")
    precision = _floating_dtype(field.values)
    values = _converted(_point_values(field.values, data.num_points), precision)
    if polyhedral:
        from tack.dataset.algorithms._clip_polyhedra import clip_polyhedra

        return clip_polyhedra(data, arrays.materialize(values), float(value), inside, fields)
    invert = 1 if inside else 0           # the tables' name: keep what is below
    n = data.num_cells

    groups = []
    for group in data.topology.groups():
        if group.count:
            t = _shape_tables(int(group.shape.ID), bool(invert))
            if t is None:
                raise NotImplementedError(f"clip has no table for {group.shape.__name__} cells")
            groups.append((group, t))
    counts = tack.empty((n,), tack.vec(_KINDS, tack.i32))
    if n:
        counts.fill(0)
    for group, (table, cases, _, remap, _, _) in groups:
        _clip_counts(group.view(), values, float(value), invert, table, cases, remap, counts)
    idt = data.id_dtype
    odt = ids.for_output(data, _MOST * n)
    starts = tack.empty((n,), tack.vec(_KINDS, odt))
    if n <= _SERIAL_KINDS:
        # A small mesh: every kind's scan in one thread, one launch and one read,
        # where the parallel scans below are eleven launches.
        sums = tack.empty((1,), tack.vec(_KINDS, odt))
        if n:
            _scan_kinds(counts, starts, sums, n)
        totals = [int(v) for v in sums.numpy().reshape(-1)] if n else [0] * _KINDS
    else:
        totals, parts = [], []
        for kind in range(_KINDS):
            part = tack.empty((n,), tack.i32)
            kind_starts = tack.empty((n,), odt)
            _split_counts(counts, kind, part)
            totals.append(exclusive_scan(part, kind_starts, n))
            parts.append(kind_starts)
        _join_starts(*parts, starts)
    n_cells, n_conn, n_records, n_centroids, n_members = totals

    types = tack.empty((n_cells,), tack.u8)
    offsets = tack.zeros((n_cells + 1,), odt)
    connectivity = tack.empty((n_conn,), odt)
    sources = tack.empty((n_cells,), idt)
    keys = tack.empty((n_records,), tack.vec(2, idt))
    slots = tack.empty((n_records,), odt)
    centroid_offsets = tack.empty((n_centroids + 1,), odt)
    centroid_cells = tack.empty((n_centroids,), idt)
    for group, (table, cases, edges, remap, whole_type, whole_order) in groups:
        _clip_emit(group.view(), values, float(value), invert, table, cases, edges, remap,
                   whole_type, whole_order, starts, types, offsets, connectivity, sources,
                   keys, slots, centroid_offsets, centroid_cells)
    _close(offsets, n_cells, n_conn)
    _close(centroid_offsets, n_centroids, n_members)

    order = key_order(keys, data.num_points, odt)
    point_runs, count = run_offsets(keys, order)
    members = tack.empty((n_members,), odt)
    ends = tack.empty((count,), tack.vec(2, idt))
    # Weights are fractions even when the values are integers (Viskores interpolates
    # an integer field's crossings the same way).
    weights = tack.empty((count,), precision)
    if count:
        _resolve_points(keys, order, point_runs, slots, values,
                        arrays.materialize(data.geometry.values), float(value), connectivity,
                        members, ends, weights, count)
    if n_conn:
        _centroid_entries(connectivity, count)
    out = UnstructuredTopology(types, offsets, connectivity, num_points=count + n_centroids)
    points = Interpolate(ends, weights, averages=(centroid_offsets, members),
                         average_cells=centroid_cells)
    return carry(data, out, points=points, cells=Pieces(sources), fields=fields)

    @on_inputs_device
def boundary_faces(data):
    """The faces with one side -- the boundary -- as a face ``Set``: a 3D mesh's
    boundary faces, a 2D mesh's boundary edges, a polyline mesh's free ends,
    numbered as ``data.topology.faces()`` numbers them. Name it in ``data.sets``
    (``data.sets["boundary"] = boundary_faces(data)``) to iterate over it or
    carry it through filters; ``extract_surface`` makes a dataset of it."""
    return Set._from_sorted_ids(data.topology, "faces", data.topology.faces().boundary())

    extract_surface ¶

    extract_surface(data, faces=None, fields=None)

    The faces -- a face Set (as boundary_faces returns), a set's name in data.sets, or face ids (a field or an array); by default the boundary (boundary_faces), VTK's external faces -- as a dataset on the same points: a 3D mesh's faces as triangles, quads or polygons, each in its side 0's outward order; a 2D mesh's edges as line cells; a polyline mesh's ends as vertex cells. By default a 2D mesh is its own surface: its cells pass through (its hidden ones left out), as VTK's geometry filter passes polygons; its boundary edges are extract_surface(data, boundary_faces(data)). Fields on faces become the surface's cell fields, and so do cell fields (Constant, values on cells), each face taking its side 0 cell's value; point fields (H1, values on points) stay on the same points. A 3D mesh's order-2 H1 fields and geometry stay order 2 on the surface, the trace of the solid's: each face's corners, edge middles and (a quad's) center are the surface cell's, so their values are gathered, not evaluated. A 2D mesh's boundary lines take an order-2 field's values at the points. The geometry must be H1: an L2 one has no shared points for the faces to stand on.

    @on_inputs_device
def extract_surface(data, faces=None, fields=None):
    """The ``faces`` -- a face ``Set`` (as ``boundary_faces`` returns), a set's name
    in ``data.sets``, or face ids (a field or an array); by default the boundary
    (``boundary_faces``), VTK's external faces -- as a dataset on the same points: a 3D
    mesh's faces as triangles, quads or polygons, each in its side 0's outward
    order; a 2D mesh's edges as line cells; a polyline mesh's ends as vertex
    cells. By default a 2D mesh is its own surface: its cells pass through (its
    hidden ones left out), as VTK's geometry filter passes polygons; its
    boundary edges are ``extract_surface(data, boundary_faces(data))``. Fields on faces become the surface's
    cell fields, and so do cell fields (``Constant``, values on cells), each face
    taking its side 0 cell's value; point fields (``H1``, values on points) stay on
    the same points. A 3D mesh's order-2 ``H1`` fields and geometry stay order 2
    on the surface, the trace of the solid's: each face's corners, edge middles
    and (a quad's) center are the surface cell's, so their values are gathered,
    not evaluated. A 2D mesh's boundary lines take an order-2 field's values at
    the points. The geometry must be ``H1``: an ``L2`` one has no shared points
    for the faces to stand on."""
    from tack.dataset.ghosts import refuse_hidden, visible

    if faces is None:
        data = visible(data)
    else:
        refuse_hidden(data, "extract_surface of chosen faces")
    if not isinstance(data.geometry.space, H1):
        raise TypeError("extract_surface keeps the points, so needs an H1 geometry")
    if faces is None and data.topology.dimension == 2:
        # A surface mesh is its own surface: its polygons pass through, as VTK's
        # geometry filter passes them.
        return carry(data, data.topology, points=Same(), cells=Same(), fields=fields)
    if faces is None:
        fresh = _fresh_boundary(data, fields)
        if fresh is not None:
            return fresh
        from tack.dataset.algorithms.boundary_faces import boundary_faces
        faces = boundary_faces(data)
    ids = _face_ids(data, faces)
    if not getattr(data.topology, "reference_cells", True):
        return _polygon_surface(data, ids, fields)
    faces = data.topology.faces()
    idt = data.id_dtype
    n = ids.shape[0]
    # Up to 4 points a face: past the topology's own bound (12 a cell) for a
    # surface of faces that share no points.
    odt = id_types.for_output(data, 4 * n)
    sizes = tack.empty((n,), tack.i32)
    starts = tack.empty((n,), odt)
    if n:
        _surface_sizes(ids, faces.kinds, sizes)
    length = exclusive_scan(sizes, starts, n) if n else 0
    types = tack.empty((n,), tack.u8)
    offsets = tack.zeros((n + 1,), odt)
    connectivity = tack.empty((length,), odt)
    if n:
        _surface_cells(ids, faces.kinds, faces.rows, starts, types, offsets, connectivity,
                       length, n)
    surface = UnstructuredTopology(types, offsets, connectivity, num_points=data.num_points)
    cells = tack.empty((n,), idt)
    if n:
        _face_cells(ids, faces.sides, cells)
    out = carry(data, surface, points=Same(), cells=Pieces(cells), faces_to_cells=Take(ids),
                fields=fields)
    if data.topology.dimension == 3:
        _keep_order_two(data, out, ids, fields)
    return out

    extract_edges(
    data, edges=None, fields=None, subdivision=None

    The edges -- an edge Set, a set's name in data.sets, or edge ids (a field or an array); by default every edge of the topology (edges()) -- as a dataset of line cells on the same points, cell i running from edge i's lower point id to its higher (edges().rows). Values on edges (Values(data, "edges")) become the output's cell values, and edge sets its cell sets; point fields (H1, values on points) and point sets stay on the same points -- an order-2 field's or geometry's values at the points, the lines being linear. Cell and face fields are left behind: an edge lies on every cell and face around it. The geometry must be H1: an L2 one has no shared points for the lines to stand on.

    subdivision=n follows a curved geometry: each edge is n line cells through n - 1 new points on the geometry's trace along it, appended after the points (edge i's from its lower point id), so a mesh's outline shows its cells as they are. The output's geometry is the points' positions and the new ones; no other field is kept, and no ghost marks. A straight geometry's edges are lines already, and are not subdivided.

    @on_inputs_device
def extract_edges(data, edges=None, fields=None, subdivision=None):
    """The ``edges`` -- an edge ``Set``, a set's name in ``data.sets``, or edge ids (a
    field or an array); by default every edge of the topology (``edges()``) --
    as a dataset of line cells on the same points, cell ``i`` running from edge
    ``i``'s lower point id to its higher (``edges().rows``). Values on edges
    (``Values(data, "edges")``) become the output's cell values, and edge sets
    its cell sets; point fields (``H1``, values on points) and point sets stay
    on the same points -- an order-2 field's or geometry's values at the
    points, the lines being linear. Cell and face fields are left behind: an
    edge lies on every cell and face around it. The geometry must be ``H1``:
    an ``L2`` one has no shared points for the lines to stand on.

    ``subdivision=n`` follows a curved geometry: each edge is ``n`` line cells
    through ``n - 1`` new points on the geometry's trace along it, appended after
    the points (edge ``i``'s from its lower point id), so a mesh's outline shows
    its cells as they are. The output's geometry is the points' positions and
    the new ones; no other field is kept, and no ghost marks. A straight
    geometry's edges are lines already, and are not subdivided."""
    from tack.dataset.ghosts import refuse_hidden, visible

    if edges is None:
        data = visible(data)
    else:
        refuse_hidden(data, "extract_edges of chosen edges")
    if not isinstance(data.geometry.space, H1):
        raise TypeError("extract_edges keeps the points, so needs an H1 geometry")
    topology = data.topology
    found = topology.edges()
    idt = data.id_dtype
    if edges is None:
        n = found.num_edges
        chosen = CountingArray(n, dtype=idt)              # every edge, in order
        edges_to_cells = Same()
    else:
        chosen = _edge_ids(data, edges, found.num_edges)
        n = chosen.shape[0]
        edges_to_cells = Take(chosen)
    types, offsets = uniform_cells(shapes.LINE, n, idt)       # all lines: implicit
    connectivity = tack.empty((2 * n,), idt)
    if n:
        _edge_cells(chosen, found.rows, connectivity, n)
    if (subdivision is not None and int(subdivision) > 1
            and data.geometry.space.order > 1):
        if fields:
            raise ValueError("extract_edges keeps only the geometry when it subdivides edges")
        return _subdivided(data, chosen, n, int(subdivision))
    lines = UnstructuredTopology(types, offsets, connectivity, num_points=data.num_points)
    return carry(data, lines, points=Same(), edges_to_cells=edges_to_cells, fields=fields)

    A surface's edges of the kinds asked for, as line cells on the same points, each from its lower point id to its higher, in order of those ids, with kind (EdgeKind) on the cells -- as VTK's vtkFeatureEdges:

    • boundary: edges of one cell;
    • feature: edges of two cells whose normals are at least angle degrees apart (two cells wound opposite ways meet at almost 180);
    • non_manifold: edges of three or more cells;
    • manifold: the other edges of two cells -- all of them when feature edges are not asked for, as in VTK (off by default).

    The surface is the 2D cells -- triangles, quads, pixels, polygons; a polygon's normal is Newell's. Other cells are left out; a volume mesh's surface comes from extract_surface first. Point fields stay on the same points (fields chooses which, as extract_edges); cell fields are left behind, an edge belonging to every cell around it. Hidden cells are left out. The geometry must be H1.

    @on_inputs_device
def feature_edges(data, angle=30.0, boundary=True, feature=True, non_manifold=True,
                  manifold=False, fields=None):
    """A surface's edges of the kinds asked for, as line cells on the same points,
    each from its lower point id to its higher, in order of those ids, with
    ``kind`` (``EdgeKind``) on the cells -- as VTK's ``vtkFeatureEdges``:

    - ``boundary``: edges of one cell;
    - ``feature``: edges of two cells whose normals are at least ``angle``
      degrees apart (two cells wound opposite ways meet at almost 180);
    - ``non_manifold``: edges of three or more cells;
    - ``manifold``: the other edges of two cells -- all of them when feature
      edges are not asked for, as in VTK (off by default).

    The surface is the 2D cells -- triangles, quads, pixels, polygons; a
    polygon's normal is Newell's. Other cells are left out; a volume mesh's
    surface comes from ``extract_surface`` first. Point fields stay on the same
    points (``fields`` chooses which, as ``extract_edges``); cell fields are
    left behind, an edge belonging to every cell around it. Hidden cells are
    left out. The geometry must be ``H1``."""
    from tack.dataset.ghosts import visible
    from tack.dataset.polyhedra import PolygonalTopology

    data = visible(data)
    if not isinstance(data.geometry.space, H1):
        raise TypeError("feature_edges keeps the points, so needs an H1 geometry")
    topology = data.topology
    if topology.dimension == 3:
        raise ValueError("feature_edges takes a surface; take a volume mesh's with "
                         "extract_surface first")
    if not 0.0 <= angle <= 180.0:
        raise ValueError(f"the feature angle is in degrees, 0 to 180, not {angle!r}")
    idt = data.id_dtype
    n_cells = data.num_cells
    # Each 2D cell's loop of point ids.
    if isinstance(topology, PolygonalTopology):
        offsets, loops = (ids.as_ids(a, idt) for a in topology.loops())
    else:
        sizes = tack.zeros((n_cells,), tack.i64)
        groups = [g for g in data.launch_groups("cells", []) if g.count]
        for group in groups:
            if group.shape in _ROUND:
                _loop_sizes(data.domain_view("cells", group), len(_ROUND[group.shape]), sizes)
        offsets = tack.empty((n_cells + 1,), tack.i64)
        total = int(exclusive_scan(sizes, offsets, n_cells, close=True))
        loops = tack.empty((total,), idt)
        for group in groups:
            if group.shape in _ROUND:
                order = _table(("round", group.shape), _ROUND[group.shape])
                _shape_loops(data.domain_view("cells", group), order, offsets, loops)
    total = int(loops.shape[0])
    positions = materialize(_point_values(data.geometry.values, data.num_points))
    keys = tack.empty((total,), tack.vec(2, idt))
    owners = tack.empty((total,), tack.i64)
    normals = _vectors(n_cells, data.dtype)
    if n_cells:
        _sides(loops, offsets, positions, n_cells, keys, owners, normals)
    count = 0
    if total:
        order = key_order(keys, data.num_points, idt)
        runs, count = run_offsets(keys, order)
    wanted = tack.array(np.array([0, boundary, feature, non_manifold, manifold], np.int32))
    kinds = tack.empty((count,), tack.i32)
    flags = tack.empty((count,), tack.i32)
    rows = tack.empty((count,), tack.vec(2, idt))
    chosen = 0
    slots = tack.empty((count,), tack.i64)
    if count:
        _classify(order, runs, keys, owners, normals, math.cos(math.radians(angle)), wanted,
                  kinds, flags, rows, count)
        chosen = int(exclusive_scan(flags, slots, count))
    connectivity = tack.empty((2 * chosen,), idt)
    kind_out = tack.empty((chosen,), tack.i32)
    if chosen:
        _chosen(flags, slots, kinds, rows, connectivity, kind_out, count)
    types, line_offsets = uniform_cells(shapes.LINE, chosen, idt)
    lines = UnstructuredTopology(types, line_offsets, connectivity, num_points=data.num_points)
    out = carry(data, lines, points=Same(), fields=fields)
    out.fields["kind"] = Field(Values(out, "cells"), kind_out)
    return out

    surface_normals ¶

    surface_normals(data, consistent=True, weights=None)

    A surface -- triangles, quads, pixels or polygons -- with its normals: the unit normal of each cell (Newell's, round its corners) as the cell field cell_normals, and at each point the cells' around it summed and made unit as the point field normals (zero at a point of no cells), as VTK's vtkPolyDataNormals computes them without splitting. With weights="area" each cell's normal is weighted by its area in the sum, so slivers -- which cut surfaces have where a crossing lands near a corner, and whose normals are far off the surface's -- count for little.

    With consistent, the polygons are first wound alike: each connected region's as its first (lowest-numbered) cell winds, by union-find over the edges on the device, the cells that wind against it turned round (their corners reversed from the first), so their normals agree -- VTK's consistency, which is on by default there too. A surface no winding makes consistent (a Moebius strip) is refused, as is an edge of three or more polygons (the mesh's faces refuse it). A polygonal topology is consistent already (it refuses to be made otherwise), so it is left as it is. The result keeps every field; the normals are dimensionless.

    @on_inputs_device
def surface_normals(data, consistent=True, weights=None):
    """A surface -- triangles, quads, pixels or polygons -- with its normals: the
    unit normal of each cell (Newell's, round its corners) as the cell field
    ``cell_normals``, and at each point the cells' around it summed and made unit
    as the point field ``normals`` (zero at a point of no cells), as VTK's
    ``vtkPolyDataNormals`` computes them without splitting. With ``weights="area"``
    each cell's normal is weighted by its area in the sum, so slivers -- which
    cut surfaces have where a crossing lands near a corner, and whose normals
    are far off the surface's -- count for little.

    With ``consistent``, the polygons are first wound alike: each connected
    region's as its first (lowest-numbered) cell winds, by union-find over the
    edges on the device, the cells that wind against it turned round (their
    corners reversed from the first), so their normals agree -- VTK's
    consistency, which is on by default there too. A surface no winding makes
    consistent (a Moebius strip) is refused, as is an edge of three or more
    polygons (the mesh's faces refuse it). A polygonal topology is consistent
    already (it refuses to be made otherwise), so it is left as it is. The
    result keeps every field; the normals are dimensionless."""
    from tack.dataset.ghosts import visible

    if weights not in (None, "area"):
        raise ValueError(f"weights is None or 'area', not {weights!r}")
    data = visible(data)
    if data.num_cells and data.topology.dimension != 2:
        raise ValueError(f"surface_normals takes 2D cells (a surface), not a mesh of "
                         f"dimension {data.topology.dimension}: extract_surface a solid "
                         "first")
    if consistent and isinstance(data.topology, UnstructuredTopology) and data.num_cells:
        data = _consistent(data)
    else:
        data = carry(data, data.topology, points=Same(), cells=Same())    # not the input
    n = data.num_cells
    cell_normals = _vectors(n, data.dtype)
    areas = tack.empty((n,), data.dtype)
    if not getattr(data.topology, "reference_cells", True):
        data.topology.faces()                      # a polygon's walk
    for group in data.launch_groups("cells", []):
        if not group.count:
            continue
        view = data.domain_view("cells", group)
        if group.shape in _ROUND:
            _shape_normals(view, _table(("round", group.shape), _ROUND[group.shape]),
                           cell_normals, areas)
        else:
            _polygon_normals(view, cell_normals, areas)
    points = tack.empty((data.num_points,), tack.vec(3, data.dtype))
    points.fill(0)
    # Each cell's normal at each of its corners, as point_links lays them out
    # (by cell and corner on shapes, by cell_points' entries elsewhere).
    if getattr(data.topology, "reference_cells", True):
        start_of, total = corner_layout(data.topology)
        corners = _vectors(total, data.dtype)
        for group in data.launch_groups("cells", []):
            if group.count:
                _corner_normals(group.view(), cell_normals, areas, int(weights == "area"),
                                start_of[group.root], corners)
    else:
        point_offsets, point_ids = data.topology.cell_points()
        total = point_ids.shape[0]
        owners = tack.empty((total,), data.id_dtype)
        if total:
            _entry_cells(point_offsets, owners)
        corners = _take(cell_normals, owners)
        if weights == "area" and total:
            _weighted(corners, owners, areas)
    if total:
        offsets, links = data.topology.point_links()
        _average_links(offsets, links, corners, points)
        _unit(points)
    data.fields["normals"] = Field(Values(data, "points"), points, "dimensionless")
    data.fields["cell_normals"] = Field(Values(data, "cells"), cell_normals, "dimensionless")
    return data

    Connectivity and winding¶

    connected_components ¶

    connected_components(
    data,
    radius=None,
    min_size=None,
    periodic=None,
    locator=None,

    Which cells are connected, through shared points: data with region, a field on its cells and one on its points, the regions numbered from 0 in order of their lowest cell id, as VTK's vtkConnectivityFilter (RegionId, all regions) and Viskores' CellSetConnectivity: region on the cells, point_region on the points. A point takes its cells' region; a point no cell uses, and a hidden cell, has -1. The largest region, or any, is a threshold of region away.

    Computed on the device: union-find over the cells and their points, each cell-point pair hooking the larger root under the smaller with an atomic minimum, then every node jumping to its root, until nothing changes.

    Over a PartitionedDataSet, regions are numbered across every piece of every rank: each piece labels its own, and pieces join the regions that meet at the points they share. With global ids on every piece, regions are numbered in order of their lowest global cell id -- the whole's numbering, for pieces carrying the whole's ids -- else of their lowest (piece, cell). With radius, the pieces are point clouds: each labels itself with copies of the other pieces' points within radius (ghost_points), and a copy joins its region to its owner's. min_size counts each point once, where it is owned.

    With radius, points within that distance of each other (inclusive) are connected too: on a point cloud, whose cells are its points, that is Euclidean clustering (VTK's vtkEuclideanClusterExtraction, PCL's) and, with the linking length, friends-of-friends halo finding (yt's FoF). min_size gives regions of fewer points -1, the rest numbered again in the same order. periodic (a box, as PointLocator takes it) joins points across its faces, as a cosmology box needs. locator reuses a PointLocator of data.

def connected_components(data, radius=None, min_size=None, periodic=None, locator=None):
    """Which cells are connected, through shared points: ``data`` with ``region``, a
    field on its cells and one on its points, the regions numbered from 0 in
    order of their lowest cell id, as VTK's vtkConnectivityFilter (``RegionId``,
    all regions) and Viskores' CellSetConnectivity: ``region`` on the cells,
    ``point_region`` on the points. A point takes its cells' region; a point no
    cell uses, and a hidden cell, has -1. The largest region, or any, is a
    ``threshold`` of ``region`` away.

    Computed on the device: union-find over the cells and their points, each
    cell-point pair hooking the larger root under the smaller with an atomic
    minimum, then every node jumping to its root, until nothing changes.

    Over a ``PartitionedDataSet``, regions are numbered across every piece of
    every rank: each piece labels its own, and pieces join the regions that
    meet at the points they share. With global ids on
    every piece, regions are numbered in order of their lowest global cell id
    -- the whole's numbering, for pieces carrying the whole's ids -- else of
    their lowest (piece, cell). With ``radius``, the pieces are point clouds:
    each labels itself with copies of the other pieces' points within
    ``radius`` (``ghost_points``), and a copy joins its region to its owner's.
    ``min_size`` counts each point once, where it is owned.

    With ``radius``, points within that distance of each other (inclusive) are
    connected too: on a point cloud, whose cells are its points, that is
    Euclidean clustering (VTK's vtkEuclideanClusterExtraction, PCL's) and,
    with the linking length, friends-of-friends halo finding (yt's FoF).
    ``min_size`` gives regions of fewer points -1, the rest numbered again in
    the same order. ``periodic`` (a box, as ``PointLocator`` takes it) joins
    points across its faces, as a cosmology box needs. ``locator`` reuses a
    ``PointLocator`` of ``data``."""
    radius = _length(data, radius, "connected_components's radius")
    periodic = _length(data, periodic, "connected_components's periodic box")
    if radius is not None and not radius >= 0:
        raise ValueError(f"radius must be at least zero, not {radius!r}")
    if isinstance(data, PartitionedDataSet):
        if locator is not None:
            raise ValueError("a PointLocator finds one piece's points; pieces take none")
        if radius is not None:
            return _components_near(data, float(radius), min_size, periodic)
        if periodic is not None:
            raise ValueError("periodic joins points within a radius across the box's faces")
        return _components_pieces(data, min_size)
    cell_region, point_region, count = _labels(data, radius, locator, periodic)
    if min_size is not None and count:
        _smallest_dropped(cell_region, point_region, count, int(min_size))
    return _with_regions(data, cell_region, point_region)

    The cells whose faces do not wind consistently, as a cell Set.

    Walking every face outward (side_point), a closed, consistently wound cell walks each of its edges exactly twice, once each way. For polygons: the cells whose edges, walked their way, do not close into a loop. Polylines have no winding, and shape-based cells take their faces from their shape's table, so are refused.

def check_winding(data):
    """The cells whose faces do not wind consistently, as a cell ``Set``.

    Walking every face outward (``side_point``), a closed, consistently wound cell
    walks each of its edges exactly twice, once each way. A cell that does not --
    a face with the wrong side, an open cell, an edge of three faces -- is listed.
    Combinatorial: geometry plays no part. For polygons: the cells whose edges,
    walked their way, do not close into a loop. Polylines have no winding, and
    shape-based cells take their faces from their shape's table, so are refused.
    """
    t = getattr(data, "topology", data)
    if getattr(t, "reference_cells", True):
        raise TypeError("check_winding checks cells that list their faces (polyhedra and "
                        "polygons); a shape's faces come from its table, wound one way")
    if t.dimension == 1:
        raise ValueError("polylines have no winding to check")
    if t.dimension == 2:
        return _check_loops(t)
    edges = t.edges()
    n = t.num_cells
    sizes = tack.empty((n,), tack.i32)
    starts = tack.empty((n,), t.id_dtype)
    if n:
        _cell_sizes(t.cell_offsets, t.cell_faces, t.face_offsets, sizes, n)
    total = exclusive_scan(sizes, starts, n) if n else 0
    bad = tack.zeros((n,), tack.i32)
    if total:
        keys = tack.empty((total,), tack.vec(2, t.id_dtype))
        directions = tack.empty((total,), tack.i32)
        _directed_edges(t.cell_offsets, t.cell_faces, t.cell_face_sides, t.face_offsets,
                        edges.face_edge, edges.face_edge_sign, starts, keys, directions, n)
        order = key_order(keys, n, t.id_dtype)
        offsets, runs = run_offsets(keys, order)
        _unbalanced(keys, directions, order, offsets, bad, runs)
    return Set._from_flags(t, "cells", bad)

    merge_points ¶

    merge_points(data, tolerance=0.0, fields=None)

    data with each set of coincident points made one: points at most tolerance apart (inclusive; 0, the default, merges only points of equal coordinates) join, and so do chains of them, so a set may span more than tolerance. A set becomes the point of its smallest id, which keeps that point's position, point fields, ghost marks and global id; the merged points keep the order of those ids, and the cells are the same cells on them, a cell's corners that merged kept as they are. Cell fields are unchanged.

    For meshes written without merging their points (each piece of a simulation's output storing a point once for every cell or block that uses it), which nothing can stitch by matching points across cells or pieces until each point is one. tolerance is in the dataset's spatial unit, or a quantity ("1e-9 m"); it should be far below the distance between points that are not copies, since every point compares itself with every point that close. Takes an unstructured topology; a structured grid's points are its lattice, and polyhedral, polygonal and polyline topologies are not handled yet. Hidden cells are dropped first, as every filter that makes cells drops them.

    @on_inputs_device
def merge_points(data, tolerance=0.0, fields=None):
    """``data`` with each set of coincident points made one: points at most
    ``tolerance`` apart (inclusive; 0, the default, merges only points of equal
    coordinates) join, and so do chains of them, so a set may span more than
    ``tolerance``. A set becomes the point of its smallest id, which keeps that
    point's position, point fields, ghost marks and global id; the merged points
    keep the order of those ids, and the cells are the same cells on them, a
    cell's corners that merged kept as they are. Cell fields are unchanged.

    For meshes written without merging their points (each piece of a
    simulation's output storing a point once for every cell or block that
    uses it), which nothing can stitch by matching points across cells or
    pieces until each point is one. ``tolerance`` is in the dataset's spatial
    unit, or a quantity (``"1e-9 m"``); it should be far below the distance
    between points that are not copies, since every point compares itself with
    every point that close. Takes an unstructured topology; a structured grid's
    points are its lattice, and polyhedral, polygonal and polyline topologies
    are not handled yet. Hidden cells are dropped first, as every filter that
    makes cells drops them."""
    tolerance = _length(data, tolerance, "merge_points's tolerance")
    if not tolerance >= 0:
        raise ValueError(f"tolerance must be at least zero, not {tolerance!r}")
    if isinstance(data.topology, StructuredTopology):
        raise TypeError("merge_points takes an unstructured topology: a structured "
                        "grid's points are its lattice")
    if not isinstance(data.topology, UnstructuredTopology):
        raise NotImplementedError(f"merge_points of a {type(data.topology).__name__} is "
                                  f"not supported yet")
    if not isinstance(data.geometry.space, H1) or data.geometry.space.order != 1:
        raise TypeError("merge_points needs an order-1 H1 geometry: one position per point")
    data = visible(data)
    topology = data.topology
    n = data.num_points
    dtype = ids.at_least(tack.i32, n + 1)
    if dtype not in get_backend().supported_atomic_dtypes:
        raise NotImplementedError(f"merging {n} points needs {dtype} atomics, which the "
                                  f"{get_backend().name} backend does not have")
    # Union-find over the points within the tolerance, through the locator's
    # bins: each pair hooks the larger root under the smaller (an atomic
    # minimum), until nothing changes, so a set's root is its smallest point
    # whatever the order of the hooks.
    labels = tack.arange(n, dtype=dtype)
    if n:
        grid = cached_point_locator(data).grid()
        every = tack.empty((n,), tack.u8)
        every.fill(1)
        changed = tack.zeros((1,), tack.i32)
        while True:
            changed.fill(0)
            _hook_near(grid, 0, every, float(tolerance), labels, changed)
            _jump(labels)
            if not int(changed.numpy()[0]):
                break
    flags = tack.empty((max(n, 1),), dtype)
    index = tack.empty((max(n, 1),), dtype)
    count = 0
    if n:
        _roots(labels, flags)
        count = int(exclusive_scan(flags, index, n))
    new_id = tack.empty((max(n, 1),), dtype)
    kept = tack.empty((max(count, 1),), dtype)
    if n:
        _numbered(labels, index, new_id, kept)
    length = arrays.size_of(topology.connectivity)
    connectivity = tack.empty((length,), data.id_dtype)
    if length:
        _renumbered(topology.connectivity, new_id, connectivity)
    merged = UnstructuredTopology(topology.types, topology.offsets, connectivity,
                                  num_points=count)
    kept = kept if count else tack.empty((0,), dtype)
    return carry(data, merged, points=Take(kept), cells=Same(), fields=fields)

def tetrahedralize(data, fields=None):
    """Every 3D cell as tetrahedra that meet face to face: two cells sharing a face
    split it along one diagonal, as VTK's vtkDataSetTriangleFilter does. A
    structured grid's hexahedra take 5 each, the two mirror splits alternating
    with the parity of (i, j, k) in the whole grid (the topology's ``offset``
    added); any other cell is the cone from its corner of smallest point id --
    global id, where ``data`` has global ids -- over the faces without it, each
    quadrilateral face split from its own smallest corner (a hexahedron or
    voxel in 6, a wedge in 3, a pyramid in 2), which fills a convex cell. So
    the pieces of a partitioned dataset split the faces they share alike too. Other cells are left out. The
    points are the same; cell fields go to each cell's tetrahedra."""

    if count:
        _fans(loop_offsets, loop_points, starts, connectivity, sources)
    return _pieces_topology(data, connectivity, sources, count, shapes.TRIANGLE, 3, fields)

    @on_inputs_device
def as_polyhedra(data, fields=None):
    """A shape-based dataset as a polyhedral one, every cell a polyhedron.

    Its derived faces already hold every face once, in side 0's outward order
    (a voxel's pixel faces as quads), with the side of each cell's reference, so
    they become the polyhedral faces as they stand: face ids, and so fields on
    faces, are unchanged. Edges come out numbered as before. Cells must be 3D,
    and neighbours wound alike: an inside-out cell beside an upright one is
    refused, since their shared face would have them on one side.
    ``Constant`` and ``H1`` order-1 fields, values on points, cells, faces and
    edges, and sets carry over; fields needing a reference element are dropped.
    """
    from tack.dataset.spaces import H1

    if not isinstance(data.geometry.space, H1) or data.geometry.space.order != 1:
        raise TypeError("as_polyhedra needs an order-1 H1 geometry: positions per point")
    topology = data.topology
    for group in topology.groups():
        if group.count and group.shape.DIMENSION != 3:
            raise ValueError(f"{group.shape.__name__} cells are not 3D: a polyhedral "
                             "topology is of 3D cells (as_polygons takes 2D ones)")
    faces = topology.faces()
    same_way = tack.zeros((1,), tack.i32)
    for group in topology.groups():
        if group.count:
            _same_way(data.domain_view("cells", group), same_way)
    if same_way[0]:
        raise ValueError(f"{same_way[0]} faces are wound the same way by both their cells "
                         "(an inside-out cell beside an upright one, as cell_geometry's "
                         "negative measures show); a polyhedral topology needs each face's "
                         "cells on opposite sides of it")
    nf = faces.num_faces
    idt = topology.id_dtype
    # The faces' points: 4 a face, past 12 a cell when faces are not shared (a
    # hexahedron has 24), and the polyhedral topology holds twice that.
    fdt = ids.at_least(idt, 8 * nf)
    sizes = tack.empty((nf,), tack.i32)
    starts = tack.empty((nf + 1,), fdt)
    if nf:
        _face_sizes(faces.kinds, sizes)
    total = exclusive_scan(sizes, starts, nf, close=True)
    face_points = tack.empty((total,), fdt)
    if nf:
        _face_rows(faces.rows, starts, sizes, face_points)

    n = data.num_cells
    counts = tack.zeros((n,), tack.i32)
    for group in topology.groups():
        if group.count:
            _cell_face_counts(group.view(), counts)
    cell_offsets = tack.empty((n + 1,), idt)
    entries = exclusive_scan(counts, cell_offsets, n, close=True)
    cell_faces = tack.empty((entries,), idt)
    cell_face_sides = tack.empty((entries,), tack.u8)
    for group in topology.groups():
        if group.count:
            _cell_face_entries(data.domain_view("cells", group), cell_offsets, cell_faces,
                               cell_face_sides)
    out = PolyhedralTopology(starts, face_points, cell_offsets, cell_faces, cell_face_sides,
                             num_points=data.num_points)

    # The same points, cells and faces (in the shape path's numbering), so the
    # sets still apply; edges too, both paths numbering them by (low, high)
    # point ids.
    return carry(data, out, points=Same(), cells=Same(), faces=Same(), edges=Same(),
                 fields=fields)
