    @on_inputs_device
def advect(data, field, seeds, step_size, steps, integrator="rk4", locator=None,
           tolerance=None, min_step=None, max_step=None, max_length=None,
           neighbors=False):
    """Seeds moved through the velocity ``field`` (a 3-vector field or its name: point
    data, cell data, or a field of any order or ``L2``, on a straight or curved
    geometry) by up to ``steps`` fixed steps of ``step_size``, as
    Viskores' ParticleAdvection: a dataset of the particles where they stopped,
    one vertex cell each, with ``steps`` (taken), ``time`` and ``status`` (the
    bits ``SUCCESS``, ``TERMINATE``, ``SPATIAL_BOUNDS``, ``TOOK_ANY_STEPS``,
    ``ZERO_VELOCITY``). ``seeds`` is an ``(n, 3)`` array or a field of
    3-vectors; ``integrator`` ``"rk4"``, ``"euler"`` or ``"rk45"`` (adaptive steps,
    with ``tolerance``, ``min_step`` and ``max_step``: see ``streamlines``);
    ``max_length`` stops a particle whose path has gone that far; ``locator``
    reuses a ``CellLocator`` of ``data``.
    ``neighbors=True`` tries the face neighbours of the cell a particle was last
    found in before searching the locator's bins: the same particles, bit for
    bit, in about half the time on large meshes, for a table of six ids a cell
    kept with the locator (``CellLocator.cell_neighbors``).

    ``seeds`` may also be what ``advect`` returned: the particles go on from
    where they stopped, with their times and the steps they took (``steps``
    counts those too), and a particle that stopped -- its steps done, at zero
    velocity, or outside -- stays as it is. A ``seed`` point field on it comes
    along.

    Over a ``PartitionedDataSet`` (``field`` by name), particles cross from
    piece to piece, in rounds: each goes to the lowest piece one of whose own
    cells (not a ghost) holds it, steps until it leaves that piece, and is
    handed on, until none is in flight on any rank.

    Each particle is one thread that takes all its steps, so on a GPU a few
    seeds use a few threads of a device built for thousands, each slower than
    a CPU core: below a few thousand seeds a CPU copy of the mesh is faster
    (the Visualization Guide's "Integrate a steady velocity field")."""
    # A step as a time ("0.5 s") is in the spatial unit over the velocity's.
    step_size, tolerance, min_step, max_step, max_length = _parameters(
        data, field, "time", "advect", step_size, tolerance, min_step, max_step, max_length)
    adaptive = {"tolerance": tolerance, "min_step": min_step, "max_step": max_step,
                "max_length": max_length}
    if isinstance(data, PartitionedDataSet):
        from tack.dataset.algorithms._particles import advect_pieces
        return advect_pieces(data, field, seeds, step_size, steps, integrator, neighbors,
                             **adaptive)
    from tack.dataset.ghosts import refuse_hidden, visible

    if locator is None:
        data, field = visible(data, field)
    else:
        refuse_hidden(data, "advect with a locator")
    seeds, resume, seed_ids = _resumed(seeds, data)
    xs, times, taken, status, _, _, _, _ = _run(data, field, seeds, step_size, steps,
                                                integrator, locator, record=False,
                                                resume=resume, neighbors=neighbors,
                                                **adaptive)
    out = _vertices(xs, data)                  # the particles stay on the device
    points = Values(out, "points")
    for name, values, unit in (("steps", taken, None), ("time", times, _time_unit(data, field)),
                               ("status", status, None)):
        out.fields[name] = Field(points, values, unit)
    if seed_ids is not None:
        out.fields["seed"] = Field(points, seed_ids.to_device(out.device))
    return out

    The paths of advect's particles, as Viskores' Streamline: each seed's positions after every step, the seed first, as one polyline per seed (a PolylineTopology), with seed (which seed's path) on the cells and time on the points. A seed that takes no step has a point and no line. The arguments are advect's.

    step_unit is what step_size measures: "time" (the default, as advect and Viskores step), or "length", an arc length along the path: the particle follows the velocity's direction, as VTK's vtkStreamTracer does by default, so slow flow takes as long steps as fast, and steps * step_size is the longest path. time is the time the particle takes either way.

    integrator="rk45" adapts the step, as VTK's vtkStreamTracer with its RK45 (Cash-Karp, vtkRungeKutta45): step_size is the first step, a step whose error estimate exceeds tolerance (a distance, in the spatial unit; 1e-6 by default) is tried again smaller, and each accepted step proposes the next, between min_step and max_step (by default a fiftieth of step_size and twice it, VTK's ratios), in step_unit. A step at min_step is taken whatever its error. max_length (any integrator) stops a path that has gone that far, its last step landing on it in the length unit.

    Over a PartitionedDataSet (field by name), paths cross from piece to piece, each piece holding the stretches it traced.

    @on_inputs_device
def streamlines(data, field, seeds, step_size, steps, integrator="rk4", locator=None,
                step_unit="time", tolerance=None, min_step=None, max_step=None,
                max_length=None, neighbors=False):
    """The paths of ``advect``'s particles, as Viskores' Streamline: each seed's
    positions after every step, the seed first, as one polyline per seed
    (a ``PolylineTopology``), with ``seed`` (which seed's path) on the cells and
    ``time`` on the points. A seed that takes no step has a point and no line.
    The arguments are ``advect``'s.

    ``step_unit`` is what ``step_size`` measures: ``"time"`` (the default, as
    ``advect`` and Viskores step), or ``"length"``, an arc length along the
    path: the particle follows the velocity's direction, as VTK's
    ``vtkStreamTracer`` does by default, so slow flow takes as long steps as
    fast, and ``steps * step_size`` is the longest path. ``time`` is the time
    the particle takes either way.

    ``integrator="rk45"`` adapts the step, as VTK's ``vtkStreamTracer`` with its
    RK45 (Cash-Karp, ``vtkRungeKutta45``): ``step_size`` is the first step, a
    step whose error estimate exceeds ``tolerance`` (a distance, in the spatial
    unit; 1e-6 by default) is tried again smaller, and each accepted step
    proposes the next, between ``min_step`` and ``max_step`` (by default a
    fiftieth of ``step_size`` and twice it, VTK's ratios), in ``step_unit``. A
    step at ``min_step`` is taken whatever its error. ``max_length`` (any
    integrator) stops a path that has gone that far, its last step landing on
    it in the length unit.

    Over a ``PartitionedDataSet`` (``field`` by name), paths cross from piece to
    piece, each piece holding the stretches it traced."""
    # A step as a time ("0.5 s") is in the spatial unit over the velocity's; as
    # a length ("1 mm"), in the spatial unit.
    if step_unit not in ("time", "length"):
        raise ValueError(f"step_unit is 'time' or 'length', not {step_unit!r}")
    step_size, tolerance, min_step, max_step, max_length = _parameters(
        data, field, step_unit, "streamlines", step_size, tolerance, min_step, max_step,
        max_length)
    adaptive = {"tolerance": tolerance, "min_step": min_step, "max_step": max_step,
                "max_length": max_length}
    from tack.dataset.partitioned import PartitionedDataSet

    if isinstance(data, PartitionedDataSet):
        from tack.dataset.algorithms._particles import streamlines_pieces
        return streamlines_pieces(data, field, seeds, step_size, steps, integrator, step_unit,
                                  neighbors, **adaptive)
    from tack.dataset.ghosts import refuse_hidden, visible

    if locator is None:
        data, field = visible(data, field)
    else:
        refuse_hidden(data, "streamlines with a locator")
    from tack.dataset.polyhedra import PolylineTopology

    _, _, _, _, (trace, trace_times), lengths, capacity, _ = _run(
        data, field, seeds, step_size, steps, integrator, locator, record=True, unit=step_unit,
        neighbors=neighbors, **adaptive)
    # Everything is chosen and numbered on the device; only counts come back.
    m = int(lengths.shape[0])
    idt = ids.for_output(data, m * capacity)
    starts = tack.empty((m,), idt)
    total = exclusive_scan(lengths, starts, m) if m else 0
    points = tack.empty((total,), tack.vec(3, data.dtype))
    point_times = tack.empty((total,), data.dtype)
    if m:
        _paths(trace, trace_times, lengths, starts, capacity, points, point_times)
    # The paths that moved, their points numbered as they are, make the chains.
    flags = tack.empty((m,), tack.i32)
    slots = tack.empty((m,), idt)
    if m:
        _moved(lengths, flags)
    lines = exclusive_scan(flags, slots, m) if m else 0
    kept = tack.empty((lines,), idt)
    seed_of = tack.empty((lines,), tack.i32)
    line_lengths = tack.empty((lines,), idt)
    if lines:
        _moved_paths(flags, slots, lengths, kept, seed_of, line_lengths)
    line_offsets = tack.empty((lines + 1,), idt)
    length = exclusive_scan(line_lengths, line_offsets, lines, close=True)
    line_points = tack.empty((length,), idt)
    if lines:
        _chains(kept, starts, lengths, line_offsets, line_points)
    topology = PolylineTopology(line_offsets, line_points, num_points=total, id_dtype=idt)
    out = DataSet(topology, points, **data._frame())
    out.fields["seed"] = Field(Values(out, "cells"), seed_of)
    out.fields["time"] = Field(Values(out, "points"), point_times, _time_unit(data, field))
    return out

    @on_inputs_device
def extract_points(data, function, inside=True, fields=None):
    """The points inside ``function``'s region (at or below zero), or outside it
    (above), as vertex cells. Needs an ``H1`` geometry: one position per point.

    The point twin of ``extract_geometry``: the points as vertex cells, with point fields
    carried and cell fields left behind (a vertex cell has no cell of the input)."""

    if not isinstance(data.geometry.space, H1):
        raise TypeError("extract_points needs an H1 geometry: one position per point")
    values = _point_values(implicit_values(data, function).values, data.num_points)
    # Outside is what is not inside: "above zero" as a range would need a bound
    # between zero and the smallest positive value, which f32 kernels (and GPUs
    # that flush denormals) do not keep.
    flags = _point_flags(data, values, -np.inf, 0.0)
    if not inside:
        _complement(flags)
    return _keep_points(data, flags, fields)

    @on_inputs_device
def threshold_points(data, field, lower, upper, fields=None):
    """The points whose ``field`` (point data: ``H1``, values on points) lies in
    ``[lower, upper]``, as vertex cells.

    The point twin of ``threshold``: the points as vertex cells, with point fields
    carried and cell fields left behind (a vertex cell has no cell of the input)."""
    field = _field(data, field)
    lower, upper = (_in_unit_of(field, v, "threshold_points' bounds") for v in (lower, upper))
    space = field.space
    if not (isinstance(space, H1) or (isinstance(space, Values) and space.on == "points")):
        raise TypeError(f"threshold_points needs point data, not {space!r}")
    if arrays.width_of(field.values):
        raise TypeError("threshold_points needs a scalar field")
    values = _point_values(field.values, data.num_points)
    return _keep_points(data, _point_flags(data, values, lower, upper), fields)

    @on_inputs_device
def mask_points(data, stride, fields=None):
    """Every ``stride``-th point (0, stride, 2 * stride, ...) as vertex cells, as
    Viskores' ``MaskPoints``.

    The point twin of ``mask``: the points as vertex cells, with point fields
    carried and cell fields left behind (a vertex cell has no cell of the input)."""
    if int(stride) < 1:
        raise ValueError(f"stride must be at least 1, not {stride!r}")
    flags = tack.empty((data.num_points,), tack.i32)
    if data.num_points:
        _every(flags, int(stride))
    return _keep_points(data, flags, fields)

A point with fewer than three neighbours, or whose neighbours lie on a line, gets a zero normal: so does one whose neighbourhood's two least spreads (variances) differ by less than 4 sqrt(eps) of the greatest, which the closed-form eigenvalues cannot tell from a line (in f32, a strip about 4% as wide as it is long).

    A normal's sign is chosen to point toward viewpoint (a world position) when one is given, else along direction (up, by default: the outside of terrain). periodic (a box) takes neighbours across its faces. locator reuses a PointLocator of data.

    @on_inputs_device
def point_normals(data, k=None, radius=None, viewpoint=None, direction=(0.0, 0.0, 1.0),
                  periodic=None, locator=None):
    """``data`` with ``normals``, each point's unit normal: the direction in which
    its neighbourhood -- its ``k`` nearest points (at most 32), itself among
    them, or the points within ``radius`` -- spreads least, from the
    eigenvectors of their covariance, as VTK's vtkPCANormalEstimation and
    PDAL's ``filters.normal``. A point with fewer than three neighbours, or
    whose neighbours lie on a line, gets a zero normal: so does one whose
    neighbourhood's two least spreads (variances) differ by less than
    4 sqrt(eps) of the greatest, which the closed-form eigenvalues cannot tell
    from a line (in f32, a strip about 4% as wide as it is long).

    A normal's sign is chosen to point toward ``viewpoint`` (a world position)
    when one is given, else along ``direction`` (up, by default: the outside
    of terrain). ``periodic`` (a box) takes neighbours across its faces.
    ``locator`` reuses a ``PointLocator`` of ``data``."""
    radius = _length(data, radius, "point_normals's radius")
    periodic = _length(data, periodic, "point_normals's periodic box")
    if (k is None) == (radius is None):
        raise ValueError("point_normals takes k or radius")
    if not isinstance(data.geometry.space, H1):
        raise TypeError("point_normals needs an H1 geometry: one position per point")
    locator = _locator(data, locator, periodic)
    n = data.num_points
    positions = locator.positions
    if k is not None:
        if not (isinstance(k, (int, np.integer)) and 1 <= k <= MAX_K):
            raise ValueError(f"k is a whole number from 1 to {MAX_K}, not {k!r}")
        nearest, _ = locator.nearest(int(k), positions)      # itself included
        # Rows of k already: CSR offsets 0, k, 2k, ..., stored nowhere.
        offsets = CountingArray(n + 1, start=0, step=int(k), dtype=data.id_dtype)
        ids = nearest.reshape((n * k,))
    else:
        if not radius >= 0:
            raise ValueError(f"radius must be at least zero, not {radius!r}")
        offsets, ids = locator.neighbors(float(radius), positions)
    if viewpoint is not None:
        toward = np.asarray(viewpoint, np.float64) - np.asarray(data.origin)
        toward_point = 1
    else:
        toward = np.asarray(direction, np.float64)
        toward_point = 0
    normals = tack.empty((n,), tack.vec(3, data.dtype))
    if n:
        # Lines' gaps reach 1.22 sqrt(eps); see _smallest_axis.
        tolerance = 4.0 * float(np.sqrt(np.finfo(data.dtype.numpy_dtype).eps))
        _normals(locator.grid(), offsets, ids, *map(float, toward), toward_point, tolerance,
                 normals)
    out = DataSet(data.topology, data.geometry, fields=dict(data.fields),
                  sets=dict(data.sets), dtype=data.dtype, **data._frame())
    out.fields["normals"] = Field(H1(out), normals, "dimensionless")
    from tack.dataset.ghosts import keep_marks

    return keep_marks(data, out)

    outliers ¶

    outliers(
    data,
    radius=None,
    min_neighbors=None,
    k=None,
    deviations=1.0,
    periodic=None,
    locator=None,
)

    data with each point marked an outlier or not: outlier, a u8 point field, 1 for an outlier. Two tests, as VTK's two filters:

    • radius (radius and min_neighbors): fewer than min_neighbors other points within radius, as vtkRadiusOutlierRemoval; neighbors gives each point's count.
    • statistical (k, at most 32, and deviations): a mean distance to its k nearest other points more than deviations standard deviations above the mean of those means, as vtkStatisticalOutlierRemoval and PCL; mean_distance gives each point's. The mean and deviation are taken in double precision on the host.

    The points are marked, not removed, as PDAL marks them (class 7): threshold_points(out, "outlier", 0, 0) keeps the rest. periodic (a box) measures across its faces. locator reuses a PointLocator of data.

    Over a PartitionedDataSet of point clouds, each piece is searched with the copies of the other pieces' points it needs (ghost_points: within radius, or its points' k nearest), and the statistical test's mean and deviation are over every piece's points: each point gets the whole's answer. The pieces come back without the copies.

    @on_inputs_device
def outliers(data, radius=None, min_neighbors=None, k=None, deviations=1.0, periodic=None,
             locator=None):
    """``data`` with each point marked an outlier or not: ``outlier``, a u8 point
    field, 1 for an outlier. Two tests, as VTK's two filters:

    - **radius** (``radius`` and ``min_neighbors``): fewer than ``min_neighbors``
      other points within ``radius``, as vtkRadiusOutlierRemoval; ``neighbors``
      gives each point's count.
    - **statistical** (``k``, at most 32, and ``deviations``): a mean distance
      to its ``k`` nearest other points more than ``deviations`` standard
      deviations above the mean of those means, as vtkStatisticalOutlierRemoval
      and PCL; ``mean_distance`` gives each point's. The mean and deviation are
      taken in double precision on the host.

    The points are marked, not removed, as PDAL marks them (class 7):
    ``threshold_points(out, "outlier", 0, 0)`` keeps the rest. ``periodic`` (a
    box) measures across its faces. ``locator`` reuses a ``PointLocator`` of
    ``data``.

    Over a ``PartitionedDataSet`` of point clouds, each piece is searched with
    the copies of the other pieces' points it needs (``ghost_points``: within
    ``radius``, or its points' ``k`` nearest), and the statistical test's mean
    and deviation are over every piece's points: each point gets the whole's
    answer. The pieces come back without the copies."""
    radius = _length(data, radius, "outliers's radius")
    periodic = _length(data, periodic, "outliers's periodic box")
    radial = radius is not None or min_neighbors is not None
    if radial == (k is not None):
        raise ValueError("outliers takes radius and min_neighbors, or k (and deviations)")
    if radial and (radius is None or min_neighbors is None or not radius >= 0):
        raise ValueError("the radius test takes a radius of at least zero and "
                         "min_neighbors")
    if not radial and not (isinstance(k, (int, np.integer)) and 1 <= k <= MAX_K):
        raise ValueError(f"k is a whole number from 1 to {MAX_K}, not {k!r}")
    if isinstance(data, PartitionedDataSet):
        if locator is not None:
            raise ValueError("a PointLocator finds one piece's points; pieces take none")
        return _outliers_pieces(data, radius, min_neighbors, k, deviations, periodic)
    if not isinstance(data.geometry.space, H1):
        raise TypeError("outliers needs an H1 geometry: one position per point")
    locator = _locator(data, locator, periodic)
    n = data.num_points
    marks = tack.zeros((n,), tack.u8)
    out = DataSet(data.topology, data.geometry, fields=dict(data.fields),
                  sets=dict(data.sets), dtype=data.dtype, **data._frame())
    points = Values(out, "points")
    if radial:
        locator.check_radius(radius)
        counts = tack.empty((n,), data.id_dtype)
        if n:
            _count_within(locator.grid(), locator.positions, float(radius), 1, counts)
            _below(counts, int(min_neighbors), marks)
        out.fields["neighbors"] = Field(points, counts)
    else:
        means = _means(locator, n, int(k), data.dtype)
        if n:
            host = arrays.to_host(means).astype(np.float64)
            limit = host.mean() + float(deviations) * host.std()
            _above(means, float(limit), marks)
        out.fields["mean_distance"] = Field(points, means, data.unit)
    out.fields["outlier"] = Field(points, marks)
    from tack.dataset.ghosts import keep_marks

    return keep_marks(data, out)

    voxel_downsample ¶

    voxel_downsample(data, size, keep='centroid', fields=None)

    One point per occupied voxel of a grid of size (a voxel's side, or three sides, in the geometry's units) anchored at the points' lower corner, as VTK's vtkVoxelGrid and PDAL's filters.voxeldownsize: vertex cells, with the input's origin.

    keep chooses the point: "centroid", the mean of the voxel's points (new points: floating-point point fields averaged, integer ones -- a classification, intensities -- the voxel's first point's); "first", the voxel's lowest-numbered point; "nearest", its point nearest the centroid (the lowest-numbered on a tie). The last two keep input points, in input order, with their fields and ghost marks. Point fields come along (fields choosing, as filters do); cell fields do not. Each voxel is reduced in index order, so the result has the same bits from run to run, and the voxels and kept points are the same on every backend: the nearest point's distances are rounded alike everywhere (squared_length), so a tie falls the same way.

    Over a PartitionedDataSet, the grid is anchored at the lower corner of every piece's points, and each voxel's owned points are brought to one block by a sort over the blocks, in order of piece and then index, and reduced there. A voxel belongs to the piece of its first point, which keeps its centroid; "first" and "nearest" keep input points on their own pieces. Each piece of the result holds its share of the whole's points.

    @on_inputs_device
def voxel_downsample(data, size, keep="centroid", fields=None):
    """One point per occupied voxel of a grid of ``size`` (a voxel's side, or three
    sides, in the geometry's units) anchored at the points' lower corner, as
    VTK's vtkVoxelGrid and PDAL's ``filters.voxeldownsize``: vertex cells, with
    the input's origin.

    ``keep`` chooses the point: ``"centroid"``, the mean of the voxel's points
    (new points: floating-point point fields averaged, integer ones -- a
    classification, intensities -- the voxel's first point's); ``"first"``,
    the voxel's lowest-numbered point; ``"nearest"``, its point nearest the
    centroid (the lowest-numbered on a tie). The last two keep input points,
    in input order, with their fields and ghost marks. Point fields come along
    (``fields`` choosing, as filters do); cell fields do not. Each voxel is
    reduced in index order, so the result has the same bits from run to run,
    and the voxels and kept points are the same on every backend: the
    nearest point's distances are rounded alike everywhere
    (``squared_length``), so a tie falls the same way.

    Over a ``PartitionedDataSet``, the grid is anchored at the lower corner of
    every piece's points, and each voxel's owned points are brought to one
    block by a sort over the blocks, in order of piece and then index, and
    reduced there. A voxel belongs to the piece of its first point, which keeps
    its centroid; ``"first"`` and ``"nearest"`` keep input points on their own
    pieces. Each piece of the result holds its share of the whole's points."""
    size = _length(data, size, "voxel_downsample's size")
    if keep not in _KEEP:
        raise ValueError(f"keep is one of {', '.join(map(repr, _KEEP))}, not {keep!r}")
    sizes = np.broadcast_to(np.asarray(size, np.float64), (3,)).astype(float)
    if not (np.all(np.isfinite(sizes)) and np.all(sizes > 0)):
        raise ValueError(f"size is a positive voxel side, or three, not {size!r}")
    if isinstance(data, PartitionedDataSet):
        return _downsample_pieces(data, size, sizes, keep, fields)
    if not isinstance(data.geometry.space, H1):
        raise TypeError("voxel_downsample needs an H1 geometry: one position per point")
    n = data.num_points
    positions = arrays.materialize(_point_values(data.geometry.values, n))
    if n:
        x = arrays.to_host(positions).reshape(-1, 3).astype(np.float64)
        low, high = x.min(axis=0), x.max(axis=0)
    else:
        low = high = np.zeros(3)
    counts = np.floor((high - low) / sizes).astype(np.int64) + 1
    if float(np.prod(counts.astype(float))) >= 2.0 ** 62:
        raise ValueError(f"{size!r} makes too many voxels over the points' box")
    keys = tack.empty((n,), tack.i64)
    if n:
        _voxel_keys(positions, *map(float, low), *map(float, sizes), int(counts[0]),
                    int(counts[1]), keys)
    order = argsort(keys)
    offsets, nruns = _run_offsets(gather(keys, order), n)
    if keep == "centroid":
        centroids = tack.empty((nruns,), tack.vec(3, data.dtype))
        if nruns:
            _run_means(positions, order, offsets, centroids)
        return _centroids(data, centroids, order, offsets, nruns, fields)
    flags = tack.zeros((n,), tack.i32)
    if nruns and keep == "first":
        _run_firsts(order, offsets, flags)
    elif nruns:
        centroids = tack.empty((nruns,), tack.vec(3, data.dtype))
        _run_means(positions, order, offsets, centroids)
        _run_nearest(positions, centroids, order, offsets, flags)
    return _keep_points(data, flags, fields)

    deposit ¶

    deposit(
    data,
    grid,
    field=None,
    reduce=None,
    method="nearest",
    per_volume=False,
)

    data's points deposited on grid, an image (uniform_grid, axis- aligned): a field on the image.

    method="nearest" puts each point in the cell holding it (nearest grid point, Viskores' ParticleDensityNearestGridPoint): the field is on the cells. method="cic" spreads it over that cell's corners by trilinear weights (cloud in cell, Viskores' ParticleDensityCloudInCell, yt): the field is on the points. Points outside the image are left out.

    Without field, each cell's (or corner's) count of points, or sum of weights. With one -- a point field of data or its name -- reduce takes "sum" (the default), "mean", "count", or, for "nearest", "min" and "max": a LiDAR surface model is the "max" of the heights on a 2D image, a terrain model the "min" of the ground's. A cell nothing reaches holds 0 for counts and sums, NaN for the rest. per_volume divides by a cell's volume (area, length on images of fewer axes): a number or mass density. Each target sums its entries in point order, so the result has the same bits from run to run. Counts, minima and maxima are the same on every backend; sums and means agree to rounding (a GPU may fuse a weight's multiply-add).

    data and grid may have different origins: the points are moved to the image's by the difference, taken in double precision.

    Over a PartitionedDataSet, each piece deposits its owned points (not the copies ghost_points adds) and the pieces' grids combine over every rank, in order of piece: sums and counts add, means divide the sums by the counts, minima and maxima take the least and the greatest. Every rank gets the whole grid's field, on grid's device; field is a name.

    @on_inputs_device
def deposit(data, grid, field=None, reduce=None, method="nearest", per_volume=False):
    """``data``'s points deposited on ``grid``, an image (``uniform_grid``, axis-
    aligned): a field on the image.

    ``method="nearest"`` puts each point in the cell holding it (nearest grid
    point, Viskores' ParticleDensityNearestGridPoint): the field is on the
    cells. ``method="cic"`` spreads it over that cell's corners by trilinear
    weights (cloud in cell, Viskores' ParticleDensityCloudInCell, yt): the
    field is on the points. Points outside the image are left out.

    Without ``field``, each cell's (or corner's) count of points, or sum of
    weights. With one -- a point field of ``data`` or its name -- ``reduce``
    takes ``"sum"`` (the default), ``"mean"``, ``"count"``, or, for
    ``"nearest"``, ``"min"`` and ``"max"``: a LiDAR surface model is the
    ``"max"`` of the heights on a 2D image, a terrain model the ``"min"`` of the
    ground's. A cell nothing reaches holds 0 for counts and sums, NaN for the
    rest. ``per_volume`` divides by a cell's volume (area, length on images of
    fewer axes): a number or mass density. Each target sums its entries in
    point order, so the result has the same bits from run to run. Counts,
    minima and maxima are the same on every backend; sums and means agree to
    rounding (a GPU may fuse a weight's multiply-add).

    ``data`` and ``grid`` may have different origins: the points are moved to
    the image's by the difference, taken in double precision.

    Over a ``PartitionedDataSet``, each piece deposits its owned points (not
    the copies ``ghost_points`` adds) and the pieces' grids combine over every
    rank, in order of piece: sums and counts add, means divide the sums by the
    counts, minima and maxima take the least and the greatest. Every rank gets
    the whole grid's field, on ``grid``'s device; ``field`` is a name."""
    if method not in _METHOD:
        raise ValueError(f"method is one of {', '.join(map(repr, _METHOD))}, not {method!r}")
    reduce = reduce or ("sum" if field is not None else "count")
    if reduce not in _REDUCE:
        raise ValueError(f"reduce is one of {', '.join(map(repr, _REDUCE))}, not {reduce!r}")
    if field is None and reduce != "count":
        raise ValueError(f"reduce={reduce!r} needs a field to reduce")
    if method == "cic" and reduce in ("min", "max"):
        raise ValueError("cloud in cell weighs each point: it sums, counts or averages")
    coordinates = grid.geometry.values
    if not isinstance(coordinates, UniformCoordinates) or coordinates.ORIENTED == 1:
        raise TypeError("deposit goes onto an axis-aligned image (uniform_grid)")
    if isinstance(data, PartitionedDataSet):
        return _deposit_pieces(data, grid, field, reduce, method, per_volume)
    unit = _unit(data, grid, field, reduce, per_volume)
    out, on = _deposited(data, grid, field, reduce, method, per_volume)
    return Field(Values(grid, on), out, unit)

    @on_inputs_device
def sph_density(particles, kernel="cubic", smoothing_length="h", mass="mass", dimension=3,
                periodic=None, locator=None):
    """``particles`` with ``density``, each particle's SPH density ``rho_i = sum_j m_j
    W(|x_i - x_j|, h_i)`` -- itself included, from its own smoothing length (the
    gather form, as SPLASH computes it) -- for particles that come without one.
    The arguments are ``sph_interpolate``'s."""
    smoothing_length = _smoothing(particles, smoothing_length)
    mass, mass_unit = _given(particles, mass, "mass")
    periodic = _length(particles, periodic, "the periodic box")
    from tack.dataset.ghosts import keep_marks

    w, support = _checked(kernel, dimension)
    if not isinstance(particles.geometry.space, H1):
        raise TypeError("sph_density needs the particles' positions: an H1 geometry")
    n = particles.num_points
    density = tack.zeros((n,), particles.dtype)
    if n:
        found = _locator(particles, locator, periodic)
        smoothing = _per_particle(particles, smoothing_length, "smoothing_length")
        found.check_radius(support * float(arrays.to_host(smoothing).max()))
        _densities(found.grid(), w, support, smoothing,
                   _per_particle(particles, mass, "mass"), density)
    out = DataSet(particles.topology, particles.geometry, fields=dict(particles.fields),
                  sets=dict(particles.sets), dtype=particles.dtype, **particles._frame())
    out.fields["density"] = Field(H1(out), density, units.derived(
        mass_unit, (particles.unit, -dimension)))
    return keep_marks(particles, out)

    @on_inputs_device
def sph_interpolate(particles, target, fields=None, kernel="cubic", smoothing_length="h",
                    mass="mass", density="density", normalize=False, dimension=3,
                    periodic=None, locator=None):
    """``particles``' point fields at ``target``'s points by SPH kernel sums: ``A(x) =
    sum_j (m_j / rho_j) A_j W(|x - x_j|, h_j)``, each particle reaching to its
    kernel's support (2, 2.5 or 3 smoothing lengths), as VTK's
    vtkSPHInterpolator and SPLASH.

    ``target`` is a dataset -- an image to resample onto, a slice, a point cloud
    -- or an ``(n, 3)`` array of world positions, which becomes vertex cells;
    the result is ``target`` with each field (``fields`` chooses; all point
    fields but the smoothing length, mass and density by default) on its points,
    and ``shepard``, the sum of the particles' ``(m / rho) W`` there: where it
    is near 1 the particles cover the point, near 0 they do not. ``normalize``
    divides by it (VTK's ShepardProcessing), which makes a constant exact near
    the particles' edge.

    ``smoothing_length``, ``mass`` and ``density`` are the particles' point
    fields (names or ``Field``s) or numbers for all of them. ``kernel`` is
    ``"cubic"``, ``"quartic"``, ``"quintic"`` or ``"wendland"``, normalized in
    ``dimension`` dimensions. ``periodic`` (a box) reaches across its faces.
    ``locator`` reuses a ``PointLocator`` of the particles. The target's points are moved to the particles' origin by the
    difference of the two, in double precision."""
    smoothing_length = _smoothing(particles, smoothing_length)
    mass, mass_unit = _given(particles, mass, "mass")
    density, density_unit = _given(particles, density, "density")
    periodic = _length(particles, periodic, "the periodic box")
    from tack.dataset.algorithms._extract import _vertices
    from tack.dataset.dataset import relative_positions
    from tack.dataset.ghosts import keep_marks

    w, support = _checked(kernel, dimension)
    if not isinstance(particles.geometry.space, H1):
        raise TypeError("sph_interpolate needs the particles' positions: an H1 geometry")
    if not isinstance(target, DataSet):
        target = _vertices(relative_positions(target, particles.origin, particles.unit), particles)
    if not isinstance(target.geometry.space, H1):
        raise TypeError("sph_interpolate needs the target's points: an H1 geometry")
    smoothing = _per_particle(particles, smoothing_length, "smoothing_length")
    reserved = {v for v in (smoothing_length, mass, density) if isinstance(v, str)}
    names = [name for name in (fields if fields is not None else particles.fields)
             if name not in reserved or fields is not None]
    n = particles.num_points
    volumes = tack.empty((n,), particles.dtype)
    if n:
        _volumes(_per_particle(particles, mass, "mass"),
                 _per_particle(particles, density, "density"), volumes)
    units.check("sph_interpolate's target and particles' spatial unit", target.unit,
                particles.unit)
    # Each term is f times m/rho, a volume, times W, per volume: m / (rho L^d) is
    # a pure number for consistent units, unknown where the mass or density is a
    # number.
    weight_unit = units.derived(mass_unit, (density_unit, -1), (particles.unit, -dimension))
    locator = _locator(particles, locator, periodic)
    m = target.num_points
    queries = arrays.materialize(_point_values(target.geometry.values, m))
    if target.origin != particles.origin:
        from tack.dataset.algorithms._moving import _shifted_values

        queries = _shifted_values(queries, target.dtype,
                                  np.asarray(target.origin) - np.asarray(particles.origin))
    if queries.dtype != particles.geometry.values.dtype:
        queries = queries.astype(tack.vec(3, particles.dtype))
    reach = support * (float(arrays.to_host(smoothing).max()) if n else 0.0)
    locator.check_radius(reach)
    out = DataSet(target.topology, target.geometry, fields=dict(target.fields),
                  sets=dict(target.sets), dtype=target.dtype, **target._frame())
    shepard = tack.zeros((m,), particles.dtype)
    grid = locator.grid()
    for name in names:
        field = particles.fields[name]
        on_points = (isinstance(field.space, H1) and field.space.order == 1) or (
            isinstance(field.space, Values) and field.space.on == "points")
        if not on_points:
            continue
        values = arrays.materialize(_point_values(field.values, n))
        scalar = getattr(values.dtype, "scalar_dtype", values.dtype)
        if scalar.numpy_dtype.kind != "f":
            continue                            # an integer field has no kernel average
        result = tack.zeros((m,), values.dtype)
        if n and m:
            _interpolated(grid, w, support, reach, queries, smoothing, volumes, values,
                          result, shepard)
            if normalize:
                _normalized(result, shepard)
        same = normalize or weight_unit == "dimensionless"
        out.fields[name] = Field(H1(out), result, field.unit if same else
                                 units.derived(field.unit, weight_unit))
    if not names and n and m:                      # no fields: the Shepard sum alone
        _interpolated(grid, w, support, reach, queries, smoothing, volumes, volumes,
                      tack.zeros((m,), particles.dtype), shepard)
    out.fields["shepard"] = Field(H1(out), shepard, weight_unit)
    return keep_marks(target, out)

    The halos of particles -- the groups of region, a point field of halo labels (connected_components' point_region: friends-of- friends with radius the linking length; -1 for no halo) -- as a point cloud of one point per halo, ported from Viskores' cosmotools and ParaView's LANL halo finder. Each halo's fields:

    • halo, its label; count; mass, the sum of its particles' (mass a point field or one number for all, as Viskores takes it);
    • com, its centre of mass;
    • mbp, its most bound particle (the index of the particle of least potential -G sum m_j / sqrt(r^2 + softening^2) over the halo), and potential, that least potential;
    • with velocity (a 3-vector point field): velocity, the mass- weighted mean, and dispersion, the one-dimensional velocity dispersion sqrt(sum m |v - mean|^2 / 3M);
    • radius, the farthest particle from the halo's point.

    The point is the MBP's position (center="mbp") or the centre of mass ("com"). In a periodic box (a side, three, or corners, as PointLocator takes it) each halo is unwrapped about its first particle before anything is summed, so a halo across a face is whole, and its points are put back in the box. Positions are relative to the particles' origin, which the catalogue shares. Every sum runs in particle order, so the result has the same bits from run to run; counts and masses are the same on every backend, the other sums agree to rounding (a GPU may fuse a multiply-add), and so the most bound particle can differ between backends only where two potentials tie to rounding.

    Over a PartitionedDataSet (labels numbered across the pieces, as connected_components numbers them), each halo's owned particles are brought to one block by a sort over the blocks, in order of piece and then index, and catalogued there: a PartitionedDataSet of catalogues, the halos in order of label across them, each mbp an index in the piece mbp_piece (a global piece id).

    @on_inputs_device
def halo_catalog(particles, region="point_region", mass=1.0, velocity=None, center="mbp",
                 softening=0.0, G=1.0, periodic=None):
    """The halos of ``particles`` -- the groups of ``region``, a point field of
    halo labels (``connected_components``' ``point_region``: friends-of-
    friends with ``radius`` the linking length; -1 for no halo) -- as a point
    cloud of one point per halo, ported from Viskores' cosmotools and ParaView's
    LANL halo finder. Each halo's fields:

    - ``halo``, its label; ``count``; ``mass``, the sum of its particles'
      (``mass`` a point field or one number for all, as Viskores takes it);
    - ``com``, its centre of mass;
    - ``mbp``, its most bound particle (the index of the particle of least
      potential ``-G sum m_j / sqrt(r^2 + softening^2)`` over the halo), and
      ``potential``, that least potential;
    - with ``velocity`` (a 3-vector point field): ``velocity``, the mass-
      weighted mean, and ``dispersion``, the one-dimensional velocity
      dispersion ``sqrt(sum m |v - mean|^2 / 3M)``;
    - ``radius``, the farthest particle from the halo's point.

    The point is the MBP's position (``center="mbp"``) or the centre of mass
    (``"com"``). In a ``periodic`` box (a side, three, or corners, as
    ``PointLocator`` takes it) each halo is unwrapped about its first particle
    before anything is summed, so a halo across a face is whole, and its points
    are put back in the box. Positions are relative to the particles' origin,
    which the catalogue shares. Every sum runs in particle order, so the
    result has the same bits from run to run; counts and masses are the same
    on every backend, the other sums agree to rounding (a GPU may fuse a
    multiply-add), and so the most bound particle can differ between
    backends only where two potentials tie to rounding.

    Over a ``PartitionedDataSet`` (labels numbered across the pieces, as
    ``connected_components`` numbers them), each halo's owned particles are
    brought to one block by a sort over the blocks, in order of piece and then
    index, and catalogued there: a ``PartitionedDataSet`` of catalogues, the
    halos in order of label across them, each ``mbp`` an index in the piece
    ``mbp_piece`` (a global piece id)."""
    softening = _length(particles, softening, "the softening")
    periodic = _length(particles, periodic, "the periodic box")
    # One mass for every particle may bring its unit ("1e10 Msun", (1e10, "Msun")).
    given_mass_unit = None
    if units.quantity(mass) is not None:
        mass, given_mass_unit = units.number_and_unit(mass)
    if center not in _CENTER:
        raise ValueError(f"center is one of {', '.join(map(repr, _CENTER))}, not {center!r}")
    if isinstance(particles, PartitionedDataSet):
        return _catalog_pieces(particles, region, mass, velocity, center, softening, G,
                               periodic, given_mass_unit)
        raise ValueError(f"center is one of {', '.join(map(repr, _CENTER))}, not {center!r}")
    if not isinstance(particles.geometry.space, H1):
        raise TypeError("halo_catalog needs the particles' positions: an H1 geometry")
    n = particles.num_points
    labels_field = particles.fields[region] if isinstance(region, str) else region
    labels = arrays.materialize(_point_values(labels_field.values, n))
    dtype = particles.dtype
    positions = arrays.materialize(_point_values(particles.geometry.values, n))
    box = periodic_box(periodic)
    if box is not None:
        lower = np.asarray(box[0]) - np.asarray(particles.origin)
        sides = np.asarray(box[1]) - np.asarray(box[0])
    else:
        lower, sides = np.zeros(3), np.zeros(3)
    order = argsort(labels)
    sorted_labels = gather(labels, order)
    offsets, nruns = _run_offsets(sorted_labels, n)
    start = 1 if nruns and int(sorted_labels[0]) < 0 else 0
    halos = max(nruns - start, 0)
    masses = _taken(_per_particle(particles, mass, "mass"), order, n)
    u = tack.empty((n,), tack.vec(3, dtype))
    run_of = tack.full((n,), -1, offsets.dtype)
    if halos:
        _unwrapped(positions, order, offsets, start, int(box is not None), *map(float, sides),
                   u, run_of)
    counts = tack.empty((halos,), particles.id_dtype)
    total = tack.empty((halos,), dtype)
    com = tack.empty((halos,), tack.vec(3, dtype))
    if halos:
        _masses(u, masses, offsets, start, counts, total, com)
    # Potentials: every pair on small halos, the pruned search on large ones.
    sizes = np.diff(arrays.to_host(offsets).astype(np.int64)) if nruns else np.zeros(0)
    large = [r for r in range(start, nruns) if sizes[r] > _EXACT]
    exact = tack.array((sizes <= _EXACT).astype(np.int32)) if nruns else tack.zeros((1,),
                                                                                    tack.i32)
    phi = tack.zeros((n,), dtype)
    g, eps2 = float(G), float(softening) ** 2
    if halos:
        _exact_potentials(u, masses, offsets, run_of, exact, g, eps2, phi)
        bounds = arrays.to_host(offsets).astype(np.int64)
        for r in large:
            _pruned(u, masses, int(bounds[r]), int(sizes[r]), g, eps2, phi, dtype)
    entry = tack.empty((halos,), offsets.dtype)
    mbp = tack.empty((halos,), tack.i64)
    potential = tack.empty((halos,), dtype)
    centers = tack.empty((halos,), tack.vec(3, dtype))
    radius = tack.empty((halos,), dtype)
    if halos:
        _least(phi, order, offsets, start, entry, mbp, potential)
        _centers(u, com, entry, int(center == "mbp"), offsets, start, centers, radius)
        _wrapped(centers, int(box is not None), *map(float, lower), *map(float, sides))
        _wrapped(com, int(box is not None), *map(float, lower), *map(float, sides))
    out = _vertices(centers, particles)
    points = Values(out, "points")
    halo_labels = tack.empty((halos,), labels.dtype)
    if halos:
        _halo_labels(sorted_labels, offsets, start, halo_labels)
    # The mass is the particles' mass field's; the potential's G is a number, so
    # its unit is unknown; labels, counts and indices are not quantities.
    mass_unit = _field(particles, mass).unit if isinstance(mass, (str, Field)) else \
        given_mass_unit
    for name, values, unit in (("halo", halo_labels, None), ("count", counts, None),
                               ("mass", total, mass_unit), ("mbp", mbp, None),
                               ("potential", potential, None),
                               ("radius", radius, particles.unit)):
        out.fields[name] = Field(points, values, unit)
    out.fields["com"] = Field(H1(out), com, particles.unit)
    if velocity is not None:
        field = particles.fields[velocity] if isinstance(velocity, str) else velocity
        v = _taken(arrays.materialize(_point_values(field.values, n)), order, n)
        mean = tack.empty((halos,), v.dtype)
        dispersion = tack.empty((halos,), dtype)
        if halos:
            _velocities(v, masses, offsets, start, total, mean, dispersion)
        out.fields["velocity"] = Field(H1(out), mean, field.unit)
        out.fields["dispersion"] = Field(points, dispersion, field.unit)
    return out

    split ¶

    split(data, pieces, ghost_layers=0)

    data, a structured grid, cut by index ranges into a PartitionedDataSet of pieces structured grids, x fastest.

    pieces is a count, factored over the axes (each prime factor, largest first, cuts the axis whose pieces have most cells), or a tuple of counts, one per axis of the topology. Each axis's cells are shared out as evenly as they go, every piece getting at least one; neighbouring pieces share the points between them. A piece keeps the geometry's kind -- uniform coordinates with their origin moved, rectilinear axes cut, explicit points taken -- and carries its block of every point, cell and L2 field and every set, as filters carry them; fields on faces or edges are left behind.

    ghost_layers adds that many layers of each neighbour's cells around a piece, as far as the grid goes, marked duplicates (DUPLICATECELL in ghosts), as VTK's vtkGhostCellsGenerator adds them. Filters need one to give each piece's share of what they make on the faces and edges pieces share. Every point has one owner: a point of several pieces' own cells is the first such piece's, x fastest, and a duplicate (DUPLICATEPOINT) in the others, as is every point of the ghost layers. The input's own ghost marks come along. An unstructured mesh is partitioned by VTK (vtkRedistributeDataSetFilter) or by its host application.

    @on_inputs_device
def split(data, pieces, ghost_layers=0):
    """``data``, a structured grid, cut by index ranges into a ``PartitionedDataSet``
    of ``pieces`` structured grids, x fastest.

    ``pieces`` is a count, factored over the axes (each prime factor, largest
    first, cuts the axis whose pieces have most cells), or a tuple of counts,
    one per axis of the topology. Each axis's cells are shared out as evenly
    as they go, every piece getting at least one; neighbouring pieces share
    the points between them. A piece keeps the geometry's kind -- uniform
    coordinates with their origin moved, rectilinear axes cut, explicit
    points taken -- and carries its block of every point, cell and L2 field
    and every set, as filters carry them; fields on faces or edges are left
    behind.

    ``ghost_layers`` adds that many layers of each neighbour's cells around a
    piece, as far as the grid goes, marked duplicates (``DUPLICATECELL`` in
    ``ghosts``), as VTK's ``vtkGhostCellsGenerator`` adds them. Filters need
    one to give each piece's share of what they make on the faces and edges
    pieces share. Every point has one owner: a point of several pieces' own
    cells is the first such piece's, x fastest, and a duplicate
    (``DUPLICATEPOINT``) in the others, as is every point of the ghost
    layers. The input's own ghost marks come along. An unstructured mesh is
    partitioned by VTK (``vtkRedistributeDataSetFilter``) or by its host
    application."""
    topology = data.topology
    if not isinstance(topology, StructuredTopology):
        raise TypeError("split cuts structured grids; partition an unstructured mesh "
                        "with VTK (vtkRedistributeDataSetFilter) or the host application")
    layers = int(ghost_layers)
    if layers < 0 or layers != ghost_layers:
        raise ValueError(f"ghost_layers is a count of layers, not {ghost_layers!r}")
    dims = topology.point_dims
    cells = tuple(d - 1 for d in dims)
    counts = _counts(pieces, cells)
    coordinates = data.geometry.values
    implicit = (isinstance(data.geometry.space, H1)
                and isinstance(coordinates, (UniformCoordinates, CartesianProduct)))
    if implicit:
        # The topology's axes are the coordinates' axes of more than one point.
        axes = [a for a, d in enumerate(coordinates.dims) if d != 1]
    device = data.device
    bounds = [[k * n // c for k in range(c + 1)] for n, c in zip(cells, counts)]
    out = []
    for index in np.ndindex(*reversed(counts)):
        index = tuple(reversed(index))                # x fastest
        own = [(b[i], b[i + 1]) for b, i in zip(bounds, index)]        # its cells
        # With its ghost layers, as far as the grid goes.
        start = tuple(max(lo - layers, 0) for lo, _ in own)
        stop = tuple(min(hi + layers, n) for (_, hi), n in zip(own, cells))
        block_cells = tuple(b - a for a, b in zip(start, stop))
        block_points = tuple(n + 1 for n in block_cells)
        piece = StructuredTopology(block_points, id_dtype=topology.id_dtype, device=device,
                                   offset=[o + s for o, s in zip(topology.offset, start)])
        geometry = None
        if implicit:
            geometry = Field(H1(piece), _block_geometry(coordinates, axes, start,
                                                        block_points, device))
        point_ids = _ids(dims, start, block_points, topology.id_dtype)
        cell_ids = _ids(cells, start, block_cells, topology.id_dtype)
        part = carry(data, piece, points=Take(point_ids), cells=Take(cell_ids),
                     geometry=geometry)
        part.ghosts = _block_ghosts(data.ghosts, point_ids, cell_ids, block_points,
                                    block_cells, start, own)
        out.append(part)
    return PartitionedDataSet(out)

    ghost_cells ¶

    ghost_cells(
    data, layers=1, world=None, fields=None, tolerance=0.0
)

    data's pieces, each with a layer of its neighbours' cells added as ghosts: a new PartitionedDataSet, as VTK's vtkGhostCellsGenerator makes.

    data holds this rank's pieces, all unstructured (UnstructuredTopology) or all structured (below), without ghost cells, on any devices; world is the tack.communication.World they live in (data.world, this process alone, by default). Pieces neighbour where they share points at exactly the same position, or with tolerance at most that far apart (in the spatial unit, or a quantity; chains of them too), for pieces whose copies of a shared point differ in their last bits. Each piece gains the cells of other pieces that use a point it shares with them (DUPLICATECELL), and their points it lacks (DUPLICATEPOINT); a point several pieces share belongs to the lowest of them, and is DUPLICATEPOINT in the others. Input marks come along: HIDDENCELL and the other bits are copied with each cell.

    Point and cell fields (H1 of order 1, Constant, values on points or cells) are carried, fields choosing them as filters do (None: all); point and cell sets keep their members, and global ids come along where every piece has them, points then matched by their ids rather than their positions. update_ghosts refreshes a field's ghost values from their owners afterwards, after a filter that is right only where it sees every neighbour.

    layers layers: the first, every filter's need, is the cells that use a point a piece shares; each further layer the cells, of any piece, that use a point of the layer before (a corner's diagonal neighbours included), as split's ghost layers and vtkGhostCellsGenerator's grow. Pieces thinner than layers cells are fine: a layer reaches past them to the pieces beyond.

    Structured pieces (StructuredTopology, each placed by its offset, together tiling a box of cells, as split's and VTK's image pieces do) stay structured: each becomes its block grown by layers cells, as far as the box goes, with its values from the pieces that own them, and its implicit coordinates grown with it.

    An AMRDataSet's boxes each grow by layers cells within their level's domain, the ghosts marked DUPLICATECELL and DUPLICATEPOINT: a ghost a sibling box holds is its value, copied (AMReX's FillBoundary); one no sibling holds takes the coarser level's -- the coarse cell's value for a cell, the coarse cell's corners' by linear weights for a point (FillPatchTwoLevels) -- and one neither holds is hidden. A grid's ghost positions are filled the same way, so rectilinear and curvilinear boxes grow too. Ghosts a finer box covers are marked refined. update_ghosts refreshes them, average_down puts fine data into coarse cells.

    def ghost_cells(data, layers=1, world=None, fields=None, tolerance=0.0):
    """``data``'s pieces, each with a layer of its neighbours' cells added as ghosts:
    a new ``PartitionedDataSet``, as VTK's ``vtkGhostCellsGenerator`` makes.

    ``data`` holds this rank's pieces, all unstructured
    (``UnstructuredTopology``) or all structured (below), without ghost cells,
    on any devices; ``world`` is the
    ``tack.communication.World`` they live in (``data.world``, this process
    alone, by default). Pieces neighbour where they share points at exactly
    the same position, or with ``tolerance`` at most that far apart (in the
    spatial unit, or a quantity; chains of them too), for pieces whose copies
    of a shared point differ in their last bits. Each piece gains the cells of other pieces that use a
    point it shares with them (``DUPLICATECELL``), and their points it lacks
    (``DUPLICATEPOINT``); a point several pieces share belongs to the lowest
    of them, and is ``DUPLICATEPOINT`` in the others. Input marks come along:
    ``HIDDENCELL`` and the other bits are copied with each cell.

    Point and cell fields (``H1`` of order 1, ``Constant``, values on points
    or cells) are carried, ``fields`` choosing them as filters do (``None``:
    all); point and cell sets keep their members, and global ids come along
    where every piece has them, points then matched by their ids rather than
    their positions. ``update_ghosts`` refreshes
    a field's ghost values from their owners afterwards, after a filter that
    is right only where it sees every neighbour.

    ``layers`` layers: the first, every filter's need, is the cells that use
    a point a piece shares; each further layer the cells, of any piece, that use
    a point of the layer before (a corner's diagonal neighbours included), as
    ``split``'s ghost layers and ``vtkGhostCellsGenerator``'s grow. Pieces
    thinner than ``layers`` cells are fine: a layer reaches past them to the
    pieces beyond.

    Structured pieces (``StructuredTopology``, each placed by its ``offset``,
    together tiling a box of cells, as ``split``'s and VTK's image pieces do)
    stay structured: each becomes its block grown by ``layers`` cells, as far
    as the box goes, with its values from the pieces that own them, and its
    implicit coordinates grown with it.

    An ``AMRDataSet``'s boxes each grow by ``layers`` cells within their level's
    domain, the ghosts marked ``DUPLICATECELL`` and ``DUPLICATEPOINT``: a ghost a
    sibling box holds is its value, copied (AMReX's ``FillBoundary``); one no
    sibling holds takes the coarser level's -- the coarse cell's value for a
    cell, the coarse cell's corners' by linear weights for a point
    (``FillPatchTwoLevels``) -- and one neither holds is hidden. A grid's ghost
    positions are filled the same way, so rectilinear and curvilinear boxes
    grow too. Ghosts a finer box covers are marked refined. ``update_ghosts``
    refreshes them, ``average_down`` puts fine data into coarse cells.
    """
    if isinstance(layers, bool) or not isinstance(layers, (int, np.integer)) or layers < 1:
        raise ValueError(f"ghost_cells makes one or more layers, not {layers!r}")
    from tack.dataset.amr import AMRDataSet

    if isinstance(data, AMRDataSet):
        from tack.dataset.algorithms.amr_ghosts import amr_ghost_cells

        return amr_ghost_cells(data, int(layers), fields)
    if not isinstance(data, PartitionedDataSet):
        raise TypeError(f"ghost_cells takes a PartitionedDataSet, not {type(data).__name__}")
    world = data.world if world is None else world
    common_origin(data, "ghost_cells", world)       # positions are matched as they are
    tolerance = _tolerance(data, tolerance, "ghost_cells")
    pieces = list(data)
    names = _carried(pieces, fields)
    for i, piece in enumerate(pieces):
        _check_piece(i, piece)
    blocks = tc.Blocks([piece.device for piece in pieces], world)
    if blocks.count > 1 << (63 - INDEX_BITS):
        raise ValueError(f"ghost_cells handles up to {1 << (63 - INDEX_BITS)} pieces")
    structured = {g: int(isinstance(p.topology, StructuredTopology))
                  for g, p in zip(blocks.local, pieces)}
    every = blocks.all_gather(structured)
    if blocks.count and all(every):
        out, plans = structured_ghost_cells(blocks, pieces, int(layers), names, _kind)
        result = PartitionedDataSet(out, world=world)
        result._ghost_plans = plans
        return result
    if any(every):
        raise TypeError("ghost_cells takes pieces all structured or all unstructured, "
                        "not a mix")

    hosts = {g: _host(piece) for g, piece in zip(blocks.local, pieces)}
    # Global ids come along where every piece has them, and points are matched
    # by them then, by position otherwise.
    numbered = {kind: bool(blocks.all_reduce({
        g: int(p.global_ids is not None and getattr(p.global_ids, kind) is not None)
        for g, p in zip(blocks.local, pieces)}, "min")) if blocks.count else False
        for kind in ("points", "cells")}

    def entry(g, piece):
        chosen = hosts[g]["candidates"]
        unmarked = np.zeros(len(chosen), np.uint8)
        if numbered["points"]:
            return (chosen, [piece.global_ids.points.numpy()[chosen].astype(np.uint64)],
                    unmarked)
        return chosen, hosts[g]["positions"][chosen], unmarked

    entries = {g: entry(g, piece) for g, piece in zip(blocks.local, pieces)}
    near = tolerance and not numbered["points"]
    partners = (_matching.match_positions(blocks, entries, tolerance) if near
                else _matching.match(blocks, {g: e if numbered["points"] else
                                              (e[0], _matching.position_bits(e[1]), e[2])
                                              for g, e in entries.items()}))
    owners = {g: _matching.owners(g, hosts[g]["num_points"], partners[g],
                                  np.zeros(hosts[g]["num_points"], bool))
              for g in blocks.local}
    if near:
        _matching.settled(blocks, owners, partners)
    needed = _needed(blocks, hosts, partners, owners, int(layers))
    sent = _ghost_parts(blocks, pieces, hosts, needed, owners, names, numbered)
    incoming = blocks.exchange(sent)

    out, receive_points, receive_cells = [], {}, {}
    for g, piece in zip(blocks.local, pieces):
        result, points_from, cells_from = _appended(g, piece, hosts[g], owners[g],
                                                    incoming[g], names, numbered, blocks)
        out.append(result)
        receive_points[g], receive_cells[g] = points_from, cells_from
    point_plan = _matching.plan(blocks, receive_points)
    cell_plan = _matching.plan(blocks, receive_cells)
    result = PartitionedDataSet(out, world=world)
    result._ghost_plans = {"points": point_plan, "cells": cell_plan}
    return result

    With radius, every point within radius of the piece's box: a filter over the points within radius (outliers' radius test, point_normals, sph_density, sph_interpolate with its kernel's reach) then gives each owned point the whole's answer. around (a PartitionedDataSet with a piece for each of data's) widens each piece's box to its own piece's points too: the targets sph_interpolate resamples onto there. With k (at most 32), every point among an owned point's k nearest, wherever it is: point_normals and outliers by the k nearest then see the whole's neighbours.

    Each copy is a vertex cell marked DUPLICATECELL at a point marked DUPLICATEPOINT, owned by the piece it came from, after the piece's own points, which keep their order. Point and cell fields come along (fields choosing, as filters do), sets keep their members, and global ids come along where every piece has them. update_ghosts refreshes a field's copies from their owners, after a per-piece filter that is right only on what a piece owns (sph_density before sph_interpolate).

    In a periodic box (as PointLocator takes it) a copy across a face is an image, moved by the box's side: run filters on the result without periodic. data holds this rank's pieces, on any devices, in world (data.world by default), on one origin, without ghosts.

    def ghost_points(data, radius=None, k=None, periodic=None, around=None, fields=None,
                 world=None):
    """``data``'s pieces, point clouds (``point_cloud``: one vertex cell per point),
    each with copies of the other pieces' points it needs appended as ghosts: a
    new ``PartitionedDataSet``.

    With ``radius``, every point within ``radius`` of the piece's box: a filter
    over the points within ``radius`` (``outliers``' radius test,
    ``point_normals``, ``sph_density``, ``sph_interpolate`` with its kernel's
    reach) then gives each owned point the whole's answer. ``around`` (a
    ``PartitionedDataSet`` with a piece for each of ``data``'s) widens each
    piece's box to its own piece's points too: the targets ``sph_interpolate``
    resamples onto there. With ``k`` (at most 32), every point among an owned
    point's ``k`` nearest, wherever it is: ``point_normals`` and ``outliers``
    by the ``k`` nearest then see the whole's neighbours.

    Each copy is a vertex cell marked ``DUPLICATECELL`` at a point marked
    ``DUPLICATEPOINT``, owned by the piece it came from, after the piece's own
    points, which keep their order. Point and cell fields come along
    (``fields`` choosing, as filters do), sets keep their members, and global
    ids come along where every piece has them. ``update_ghosts`` refreshes a
    field's copies from their owners, after a per-piece filter that is right
    only on what a piece owns (``sph_density`` before ``sph_interpolate``).

    In a ``periodic`` box (as ``PointLocator`` takes it) a copy across a face is
    an image, moved by the box's side: run filters on the result without
    ``periodic``. ``data`` holds this rank's pieces, on any devices, in
    ``world`` (``data.world`` by default), on one origin, without ghosts."""
    radius = _length(data, radius, "ghost_points' radius")
    periodic = _length(data, periodic, "ghost_points' periodic box")
    ghosted = _ghosted(data, radius, k, periodic, around, fields, world)
    result = PartitionedDataSet(ghosted.pieces, world=ghosted.blocks.world)
    result._ghost_plans = {"points": ghosted.plan, "cells": ghosted.plan}
    return result

    def update_ghosts(data, *fields):
    """Copy the named fields' values on ghost points and cells from the pieces that
    own them, in place, for a ``PartitionedDataSet`` that ``ghost_cells`` or
    ``ghost_points`` made.

    A filter that needs each entity's neighbours -- ``project`` to points, point
    gradients -- is right on what a piece owns and wrong on the ghost layer's
    rim; refreshing the ghosts makes a second such filter right too. Each named
    field is a point or cell field of explicit values on every piece. One
    exchange moves all the point fields, one all the cell fields."""
    from tack.dataset.amr import AMRDataSet

    if isinstance(data, AMRDataSet):
        from tack.dataset.algorithms.amr_ghosts import amr_update_ghosts

        amr_update_ghosts(data, fields)
        return
    plans = getattr(data, "_ghost_plans", None)
    if plans is None:
        raise ValueError("update_ghosts needs the PartitionedDataSet ghost_cells or "
                         "ghost_points made, which keeps the exchanges")
    pieces = list(data)
    blocks = plans["points"].blocks
    by_kind = {"points": {g: {} for g in blocks.local}, "cells": {g: {} for g in blocks.local}}
    for name in fields:
        for g, piece in zip(blocks.local, pieces):
            if name not in piece.fields:
                raise KeyError(f"partition {g - blocks.local.start} has no field {name!r}")
            field = piece.fields[name]
            kind = _kind(field)
            if kind is None:
                raise TypeError(f"update_ghosts refreshes point and cell fields; {name!r} "
                                f"is in {field.space!r}")
            if not isinstance(field.values, tack.Array):
                raise TypeError(f"update_ghosts writes the values in place; {name!r} holds "
                                f"a {type(field.values).__name__}, not a Tack array")
            by_kind[kind][g][name] = field.values
    for kind, values in by_kind.items():
        if any(values.values()):
            plans[kind].run(values)

    data without its ghost cells -- the cells another piece owns (DUPLICATECELL) and the hidden ones (HIDDENCELL) -- and the points no remaining cell uses, as VTK's vtkRemoveGhosts: the last step before rendering, writing one file, or handing a piece to code that does not know ghost marks. Filters keep the ghost layers' output, which the next filter near a piece's edge needs, until this.

    The points kept keep their marks: a point a piece shares with another is still that one's, so reductions still count it once. A point this piece owns stays even when only ghost cells used it (a point a filter made on an edge goes to the piece owning the edge's smallest point, whose cells there may all be ghosts), so every point keeps its one owner.     @on_inputs_device
def remove_ghosts(data, fields=None):
    """``data`` without its ghost cells -- the cells another piece owns
    (``DUPLICATECELL``) and the hidden ones (``HIDDENCELL``) -- and the points no
    remaining cell uses, as VTK's vtkRemoveGhosts: the last step before
    rendering, writing one file, or handing a piece to code that does not know
    ghost marks. Filters keep the ghost layers' output, which the next filter
    near a piece's edge needs, until this.

    The points kept keep their marks: a point a piece shares with another is
    still that one's, so reductions still count it once. A point this piece
    owns stays even when only ghost cells used it (a point a filter made on an
    edge goes to the piece owning the edge's smallest point, whose cells there
    may all be ghosts), so every point keeps its one owner. A structured grid
    whose remaining cells are a block stays a structured grid; otherwise the
    cells are kept as ``extract_cells`` keeps them. ``data`` itself comes back
    when it has no ghost cells."""
    if data._ghosts_lost:
        raise ValueError("this dataset is a filter's output that lost its input's ghost "
                         "marks, so which of its cells are ghosts is not known")
    ghosts = data.ghosts
    if ghosts is None or ghosts.cells is None:
        return data
    keep = tack.empty((data.num_cells,), tack.i32)
    if data.num_cells:
        _unmarked(ghosts.cells, Ghosts.SKIPPED_CELLS, keep)
    owned = None
    if ghosts.points is not None:
        owned = tack.empty((data.num_points,), tack.i32)
        if data.num_points:
            _unmarked(ghosts.points, Ghosts.DUPLICATEPOINT, owned)
    if isinstance(data.topology, StructuredTopology):
        block = _kept_block(data, keep, owned)
        if block is not None:
            return block
    return _keep_cells(data, keep, fields, keep_points=owned)

    generate_global_ids ¶

    generate_global_ids(data, world=None, tolerance=0.0)

    data's pieces numbered across every piece, as VTK's vtkGenerateGlobalIds: a new PartitionedDataSet of the same pieces with global_ids (tack.dataset.GlobalIds), every point and cell one id, the same on every piece holding it.

    Each piece numbers what it owns in its own order, after the pieces before it -- piece 0's owned points from 0, then piece 1's -- and copies take their owner's ids. Owners come from the ghost marks where pieces have them (a copy marked DUPLICATEPOINT or DUPLICATECELL is another piece's); a point several pieces hold unmarked, as pieces without ghost cells share their boundary points, belongs to the lowest of them, and is marked DUPLICATEPOINT in the others, as VTK marks it. Points are copies of each other when their positions are exactly equal -- or, with tolerance, at most that far apart (in the spatial unit, or a quantity), chains of them too, for pieces whose copies of a shared point differ in their last bits -- and cells when their points' global ids are; pieces from ghost_cells reuse the exchanges it kept instead of matching again. Points a piece repeats within itself stay apart: merge_points merges them first.

    data holds this rank's pieces, on any devices; world is the tack.communication.World they live in (data.world by default). The matching runs on the host and the exchanges on the pieces' devices.

    def generate_global_ids(data, world=None, tolerance=0.0):
    """``data``'s pieces numbered across every piece, as VTK's
    ``vtkGenerateGlobalIds``: a new ``PartitionedDataSet`` of the same pieces with
    ``global_ids`` (``tack.dataset.GlobalIds``), every point and cell one id,
    the same on every piece holding it.

    Each piece numbers what it owns in its own order, after the pieces before
    it -- piece 0's owned points from 0, then piece 1's -- and copies take their
    owner's ids. Owners come from the ghost marks where pieces have them (a
    copy marked ``DUPLICATEPOINT`` or ``DUPLICATECELL`` is another piece's);
    a point several pieces hold unmarked, as pieces without ghost cells share
    their boundary points, belongs to the lowest of them, and is marked
    ``DUPLICATEPOINT`` in the others, as VTK marks it. Points are copies of
    each other when their positions are exactly equal -- or, with
    ``tolerance``, at most that far apart (in the spatial unit, or a
    quantity), chains of them too, for pieces whose copies of a shared point
    differ in their last bits -- and cells when their points' global ids are;
    pieces from ``ghost_cells`` reuse the exchanges it kept instead of
    matching again. Points a piece repeats within itself stay apart:
    ``merge_points`` merges them first.

    ``data`` holds this rank's pieces, on any devices; ``world`` is the
    ``tack.communication.World`` they live in (``data.world`` by default).
    The matching runs on the host and the exchanges on the pieces' devices.
    """
    if not isinstance(data, PartitionedDataSet):
        raise TypeError(f"generate_global_ids takes a PartitionedDataSet, not "
                        f"{type(data).__name__}")
    world = data.world if world is None else world
    common_origin(data, "generate_global_ids", world)
    tolerance = _tolerance(data, tolerance, "generate_global_ids")
    pieces = list(data)
    blocks = tc.Blocks([piece.device for piece in pieces], world)
    plans = getattr(data, "_ghost_plans", None)
    marks = {g: _marks(piece) for g, piece in zip(blocks.local, pieces)}

    # Points: who owns each, then the owners' numbers, then the copies'.
    if plans is not None:
        point_plan = plans["points"]
        point_owned = {g: (marks[g][1] & Ghosts.DUPLICATEPOINT) == 0 for g in blocks.local}
        point_shared = None
    else:
        point_owned, point_plan, point_shared = _point_owners(blocks, pieces, marks,
                                                                 tolerance)
    point_ids = _numbered(blocks, pieces, point_owned, point_plan, "points")

    # Cells: owned cells numbered, ghost cells from their owners.
    cell_owned = {g: (marks[g][0] & Ghosts.DUPLICATECELL) == 0 for g in blocks.local}
    copies = blocks.all_reduce({g: int((~cell_owned[g]).sum()) for g in blocks.local})
    if plans is not None:
        cell_plan = plans["cells"]
    elif copies:
        cell_plan = _cell_owners(blocks, pieces, marks, point_ids, point_shared)
    else:
        cell_plan = None
    cell_ids = _numbered(blocks, pieces, cell_owned, cell_plan, "cells")

    out = []
    for g, piece in zip(blocks.local, pieces):
        points = marks[g][1] | np.where(point_owned[g], 0,
                                        Ghosts.DUPLICATEPOINT).astype(np.uint8)
        with blocks.device(g):
            ghosts = piece.ghosts
            if not np.array_equal(points, marks[g][1]):     # copies newly marked
                ghosts = Ghosts(cells=None if ghosts is None else ghosts.cells, points=points)
            copy = DataSet(piece.topology, piece.geometry, fields=dict(piece.fields),
                           sets=dict(piece.sets), dtype=piece.dtype, ghosts=ghosts,
                           global_ids=GlobalIds(cells=cell_ids[g], points=point_ids[g]),
                           **piece._frame())
        copy._ghosts_lost = piece._ghosts_lost
        out.append(copy)
    result = PartitionedDataSet(out, world=world)
    if plans is not None:
        result._ghost_plans = plans
    return result

    data's pieces as one dataset: every cell a piece owns, once, and every point once, with the point and cell fields (fields choosing them as filters do), as VTK's vtkMergeBlocks after vtkRemoveGhosts.

    Copies of a point several pieces hold become one point, matched as generate_global_ids matches them (the ghost marks' owners, else exact positions, or positions at most tolerance apart); ghost cells are left out, and hidden cells kept, marked. The points and cells are numbered as generate_global_ids numbers them: each piece's owned ones after the pieces before it. The pieces' own global ids, if they have them, come along as the result's.

    def merge_pieces(data, root=0, fields=None, device=None, tolerance=0.0):
    """``data``'s pieces as one dataset: every cell a piece owns, once, and every point
    once, with the point and cell fields (``fields`` choosing them as filters
    do), as VTK's vtkMergeBlocks after vtkRemoveGhosts.

    Copies of a point several pieces hold become one point, matched as
    ``generate_global_ids`` matches them (the ghost marks' owners, else exact
    positions, or positions at most ``tolerance`` apart); ghost cells are left out, and hidden cells kept, marked. The
    points and cells are numbered as ``generate_global_ids`` numbers them:
    each piece's owned ones after the pieces before it. The pieces' own global
    ids, if they have them, come along as the result's.

    Structured pieces that tile a box of cells (each placed by its
    ``topology.offset``) give one structured grid of the box -- ``split``'s
    input back -- with its offset and its coordinates (uniform, rectilinear
    or explicit); other pieces give an unstructured dataset.

    Across MPI ranks every rank passes its pieces and the result is on the
    ``root`` rank (``None`` elsewhere), on ``device`` (by default the device
    of the root rank's first piece)."""
    if not isinstance(data, PartitionedDataSet):
        raise TypeError(f"merge_pieces takes a PartitionedDataSet, not {type(data).__name__}")
    from tack.dataset.algorithms.ghost_cells import _carried, _kind

    pieces = list(data)
    names = _carried(pieces, fields, "merge_pieces")
    common_origin(data, "merge_pieces")
    tolerance = _tolerance(data, tolerance, "merge_pieces")
    blocks = tc.Blocks([piece.device for piece in pieces], data.world)
    world = blocks.world
    if not 0 <= root < world.size:
        raise ValueError(f"root is a rank, 0 to {world.size - 1}, not {root}")
    firsts = blocks.all_gather({g: g == blocks.local.start for g in blocks.local})
    starts = [g for g, first in enumerate(firsts) if first]
    target = next((g for g in starts if blocks.rank_of(g) == root), None)
    if target is None:
        raise ValueError(f"merge_pieces gathers onto a piece of rank {root}, which has none")
    on_root = target in blocks.local
    out_device = (tack.device(device) if device is not None else
                  blocks.device(target)) if on_root else None
    structured = blocks.all_gather({g: isinstance(p.topology, StructuredTopology)
                                    for g, p in zip(blocks.local, pieces)})
    if all(structured):
        tiled = _box(blocks, pieces)
        if tiled is not None:
            return _merged_structured(blocks, pieces, names, _kind, target, out_device,
                                      tiled)
    return _merged_unstructured(blocks, pieces, names, _kind, target, out_device,
                                tolerance)

    def average_down(amr, field):
    """Put the finer levels' data into the coarse cells and points they cover, in
    place, as AMReX's ``average_down``: each refined coarse cell (``REFINEDCELL``)
    takes the volume-weighted average of the fine cells over it, each refined
    coarse point (``REFINEDPOINT``) the value of the fine point at its location.
    ``field`` names a floating-point point or cell field every box has; finest
    level first, so a value reaches the coarsest level in one call."""
    from tack.dataset.algorithms.cell_geometry import cell_geometry
    from tack.dataset.algorithms.ghost_cells import _kind

    if not isinstance(amr, AMRDataSet):
        raise TypeError(f"average_down takes an AMRDataSet, not {type(amr).__name__}")
    boxes = [box for _, box in amr]
    kinds = {_kind(box.fields[field]) for box in boxes}
    if len(kinds) != 1 or None in kinds:
        raise TypeError(f"average_down averages a point or cell field; {field!r} is not one")
    kind = kinds.pop()
    layout = _Layout(amr)
    d = amr.dimension
    for level in range(amr.num_levels - 2, -1, -1):
        rows = {}
        for g, (lv, k) in zip(layout.blocks.local, layout.local):
            rows[g] = _down_rows(amr, layout, lv, k, kind, d) if lv == level else \
                (_extent_size(amr._extents[lv][k], kind, d), np.zeros(0, np.int64), [])
        fill = _Fill(layout.blocks, rows)
        values = {g: box.fields[field].values for g, box in zip(layout.blocks.local, boxes)}
        for g, array in values.items():
            scalar = getattr(array.dtype, "scalar_dtype", array.dtype)
            if not isinstance(array, tack.Array) or scalar.numpy_dtype.kind != "f":
                raise TypeError(f"average_down averages floating-point values of explicit "
                                f"arrays; {field!r} is not one")
        if kind == "points":
            fill.run(values)
            continue
        # Cells: sums of measure times value over sums of measure.
        weighted, measures = {}, {}
        for g, box in zip(layout.blocks.local, boxes):
            with box.device:
                measures[g] = arrays.materialize(cell_geometry(box).measure.values)
                weighted[g] = _times(values[g], measures[g])
        fill.run(weighted)
        fill.run(measures)
        for g in layout.blocks.local:
            targets = fill.boxes[g]["targets"]
            if len(targets):
                with layout.blocks.device(g):
                    _divide(weighted[g], measures[g], tack.array(targets, tack.i64), values[g])
